questions.scope: US domestic registrant parent and assumed controlled operating subsidiary; 2025 synthetic close; separate financial-reporting and federal tax purposes.
questions.answer: Reconcile both entities by agreement, counterparty, principal, currency, rate and accrual period. The fixture assumes a 6% annual rate on unchanged principal for one full year. questions.question: When does a management-service charge differ from passive holding activity?
questions.scope: US domestic registrant parent and assumed controlled operating subsidiary; 2025 synthetic close; separate financial-reporting and federal tax purposes.
questions.answer: Document the actual service and recipient benefit before choosing a cost driver. For controlled-service tax analysis, exclude activities whose sole effect protects the shareholder investment or meets the renderer-specific obligations; day-to-day management can differ. The original allocation case uses documented processing units, retains the renderer share and separates internal allocation from tax-method and markup conclusions. The charge and receipt are reciprocal entity entries, then eliminated within the assumed group.

questions.question: How does a family office define ownership and reporting boundaries?
questions.scope: US office service company, domestic investment LLC taxed as a partnership, Texas domestic non-grantor complex trust, and individual; synthetic September 2026 close. Tax coordination uses explicitly selected 2025 IRS instructions as prior-year routing, not 2026 return instructions.
questions.answer: Maintain separate office-company, individual, trust/estate, investment-entity and underlying property or operating ledgers. The historical SEC exclusion has client, ownership/control and public-holding-out conditions; a multifamily office cannot assume the single-family exclusion.

questions.question: Which family office taxpayer and year should receive K-1, basis and estate/gift information?
questions.scope: US office service company, domestic investment LLC taxed as a partnership, Texas domestic non-grantor complex trust, and individual; synthetic September 2026 close. Tax coordination uses explicitly selected 2025 IRS instructions as prior-year routing, not 2026 return instructions.
questions.answer: Use separate taxpayer and tax-year identifiers. The investment partnership issues partner K-1 information; the individual and trust receive their own shares, including income not distributed. Maintain outside basis independently from K-1 capital. The non-grantor trust uses the fiduciary return and beneficiary K-1 route, while the individual uses the individual return and the assumed office C corporation retains its corporate route. No filing requirement, tax amount or planning action is determined.

questions.question: How can a family office reconcile a supplemental family statement without double counting?
questions.scope: US office service company, domestic investment LLC taxed as a partnership, Texas domestic non-grantor complex trust, and individual; synthetic September 2026 close. Tax coordination uses explicitly selected 2025 IRS instructions as prior-year routing, not 2026 return instructions.
questions.answer: Complete separate bank, custodian and ledger reconciliations, then define the included accounts and purpose of a supplemental view. Remove duplicated interests only where the underlying entity is also included, match interentity balances, and distinguish internal fees and beneficiary transfers from external activity. Retain the entity trial balances and an adjustment log. The original four-entity example shows a balanced carrying-value aggregation, including restricted trust resources and an unresolved valuation exception; it is not an individual’s net worth or a final GAAP financial statement. Payment-authority and sensitive-data controls are editorial proposals.

sources.summary: A survey of 373 senior internal-audit leaders covers AI-enabled fraud risk, readiness, and internal-audit use. Vendor partnership, regional selection, and self-report mean preparedness perceptions are not fraud-detection performance.

sources.title: Running payroll: Reporting to HMRC — Full Payment Submission
sources.summary: HMRC explains Full Payment Submission timing, payment-date reporting, corrections, and the employee information reported through payroll software.

sources.title: ASU 2014-09: original revenue recognition amendments, Section A
sources.summary: Sets out over-time criteria, progress measurement and contract-balance presentation; input measures may require adjustment for costs that do not depict performance.

sources.title: ASU 2018-17: common-control consolidation alternative
sources.summary: Allows qualifying private companies to elect an alternative to VIE analysis for qualifying common-control entities, while other consolidation guidance and disclosures remain applicable.

sources.summary: Official IFRS Foundation page was opened and the standard scope and recognition or classification summary were read.

sources.summary: GST/HST registration, taxable supplies, input tax credits and filing/remittance guidance for registrants.

sources.title: FASB ASU 2018-08: contributions, exchange transactions and conditions
sources.summary: FASB amendment distinguishes reciprocal exchange transactions from contributions and makes a contribution conditional only when an agreement includes both a barrier and a right of return or release.

sources.title: FASB ASU 2016-14: NFP presentation, restrictions and functional expenses
sources.summary: FASB amendment establishes two net-asset classes, donor-restriction release presentation, liquidity disclosures, endowment disclosures and expense reporting by nature and function for not-for-profit entities.

sources.title: IRS 2025 Form 990 instructions: functional expenses and federal reporting
sources.summary: IRS instructions route selected Form 990 schedules from Part IV, define endowment and donated-service reporting boundaries, and require covered exempt organizations to report functional expenses and document reasonable allocation methods; federal tax reporting can differ from financial-statement GAAP.

sources.title: FASB ASU 2015-02: Consolidation
sources.summary: Official FASB Accounting Standards Update simplifying the US GAAP consolidation analysis around voting-interest and variable-interest models. The retained synthesis is limited to the cited Topic 810 control and transition paragraphs.

sources.title: FASB Statement 57: related-party disclosure research
sources.summary: Relationships, transactions, balances and settlement terms require distinct evidence. An arm's-length claim needs substantiation; some control relationships matter without transactions.

sources.title: 2025 Instructions for Form 1120, U.S. Corporation Income Tax Return
sources.summary: Current IRS instructions for a 2025 Form 1120 return, including who must file, the period covered, signature and filing mechanics, and Schedule M-1 or M-3 book-to-tax reconciliation context.

sources.title: 2025 Instructions for Form 1042, Annual Withholding Tax Return for U.S. Source Income of Foreign Persons
sources.summary: IRS instructions for the withholding agent's annual Form 1042 reporting, including the relationship to Form 1042-S reconciliation and the reporting-year boundary.

sources.title: 2026 Instructions for Form 1042-S, Foreign Person's U.S. Source Income Subject to Withholding
sources.summary: Current IRS instructions for Form 1042-S reporting, including recipient reporting, filing timing, e-file and amendment mechanics, and the need to preserve payment-character and recipient evidence.

sources.title: Form W-8BEN-E, Certificate of Status of Beneficial Owner for United States Tax Withholding and Reporting
sources.summary: IRS source for the foreign-entity certificate used in chapter 3 and chapter 4 withholding and reporting workflows, subject to validation of status, completeness, validity, and the payment facts.

sources.title: IRS Presumption Rules for Chapter 3 and Chapter 4 Withholding
sources.summary: IRS presumption-rule guidance identifying documentation and status branches that apply when required withholding documentation is missing, incomplete, or unreliable.

sources.title: FASB ASU 2016-01: Recognition and Measurement of Financial Assets and Financial Liabilities
sources.summary: The Update generally measures equity investments within its scope at fair value through net income and provides a measurement alternative for equity securities without readily determinable fair value, subject to the stated impairment and observable-price-change requirements.

sources.title: FASB Accounting Standards Codification Topic 815: Derivatives and Hedging locator
sources.summary: The locator identifies the authorized US GAAP paragraphs for determining whether a contract or embedded feature is a derivative and for documenting hedge accounting designations.

sources.title: FASB ASU 2020-06: Accounting for Convertible Instruments and Contracts in an Entity's Own Equity
sources.summary: The Update removes specified beneficial-conversion and cash-conversion separation models for issuers while retaining derivative and own-equity classification gates, and it changes diluted EPS guidance for certain instruments.

sources.title: ARB 51 as amended by FAS 160: historical consolidation procedures
sources.summary: Historical amended consolidation procedures identify the group as one economic entity and address intercompany balances, transactions and parent-company presentation.
sources.publisher: AICPA Committee on Accounting Procedure; amended text hosted by FASB

sources.title: 2025 controlled-services regulation: allocation, benefit and shareholder activities
sources.summary: Dated federal tax text connects controlled services to a recipient benefit, identifies cost-allocation considerations and distinguishes shareholder or passive association activities.
sources.publisher: Internal Revenue Service and Treasury via GovInfo

sources.title: IRS exempt-organization gaming and unrelated business taxable income
sources.summary: IRS guidance routes exempt-organization gaming through unrelated-business-income factors and exceptions, including bingo, volunteer labor, public entertainment and member or nonmember distinctions. It also calls for separate gross gaming receipts and prize/disbursement records.

sources.title: IRS Publication 926: household employer tax route
sources.summary: IRS household-employer guidance helps determine whether a household worker is an employee and whether federal Social Security, Medicare, FUTA or withholding obligations and Schedule H reporting apply.

sources.title: SEC Family Offices final rule, published 2011
sources.summary: The published rule excludes qualifying family offices from the Advisers Act investment-adviser definition using client, ownership/control and public-holding-out conditions. Its multifamily discussion does not extend that exclusion to offices serving multiple families.

sources.title: Texas Property Code Chapter 116: selected principal and income provisions
sources.summary: The selected provisions prioritize the governing instrument, separate specified principal and income receipts, and split accounting expenses involving both income and remainder interests. The allocation rules do not determine federal taxable income.
sources.source_type: Texas fiduciary principal and income law

sources.title: IRS 2025 partner instructions for Schedule K-1 (Form 1065)
sources.summary: Partner reporting can arise without a cash distribution. The partner must maintain adjusted outside basis; a K-1 capital account is not automatically that basis.

sources.title: IRS 2025 Form 1041 instructions for estates and trusts
sources.summary: Fiduciary accounting income under the instrument and local law enters a separate federal calculation. Schedule B and DNI help determine the distribution deduction and beneficiary reporting; cash paid alone does not settle tax character.
sources.source_type: US federal fiduciary income tax guidance

sources.title: IRS 2025 beneficiary instructions for Schedule K-1 (Form 1041)

questions.question: How does a family office define ownership and reporting boundaries?
questions.scope: US office service company, domestic investment LLC taxed as a partnership, Texas domestic non-grantor complex trust, and individual; synthetic September 2026 close. Tax coordination uses explicitly selected 2025 IRS instructions as prior-year routing, not 2026 return instructions.
questions.answer: Maintain separate office-company, individual, trust/estate, investment-entity and underlying property or operating ledgers. questions.question: How can a family office reconcile a supplemental family statement without double counting?
questions.scope: US office service company, domestic investment LLC taxed as a partnership, Texas domestic non-grantor complex trust, and individual; synthetic September 2026 close. Tax coordination uses explicitly selected 2025 IRS instructions as prior-year routing, not 2026 return instructions.
questions.answer: Complete separate bank, custodian and ledger reconciliations, then define the included accounts and purpose of a supplemental view. Retain the entity trial balances and an adjustment log. Payment-authority and sensitive-data controls are editorial proposals.

sources.title: IAS 36, Impairment of Assets

sources.title: Interactivity and Illusions of Ability: How Using Generative AI Affects Investor Judgments
sources.summary: Interactive GenAI interfaces increased users' self-assessed ability and, in some tasks, hindered processing or inflated willingness to invest. The participants were investors in controlled tasks, so transfer to accountant review interfaces is a design warning rather than direct accounting evidence.

sources.title: Accounting Matters
sources.summary: Indexes FERC Uniform Systems of Accounts, forms, orders, and Chief Accountant guidance for electric, gas, and oil-pipeline entities. These regulatory requirements are industry-specific and do not establish an AI-agent design.

sources.title: 2 CFR Part 200, Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards
sources.summary: Current eCFR Part 200 requires federal-award costs to be necessary, reasonable, allocable, consistently treated, GAAP-based where applicable, documented, and not double charged; §§200.302, 200.328, 200.329 and 200.501 provide selected financial-management, reporting, performance-monitoring and audit-routing requirements. It is an external federal-award rule, not a general internal management-accounting standard.

sources.title: CMS hospital cost-report instructions — Transmittal 25
sources.summary: The 2026 hospital cost-report revision records worksheet changes and separate electronic-specification effective dates.

sources.title: ASU 2014-09: original revenue recognition amendments, Section A
sources.summary: Sets out over-time criteria, progress measurement and contract-balance presentation; input measures may require adjustment for costs that do not depict performance.

sources.title: ASU 2023-05: joint venture formations
sources.summary: Introduces recognition and initial measurement requirements in a joint venture’s own financial statements at formation.

sources.title: ASU 2018-17: common-control consolidation alternative
sources.summary: Allows qualifying private companies to elect an alternative to VIE analysis for qualifying common-control entities, while other consolidation guidance and disclosures remain applicable.

sources.title: 2022 NAICS United States manual: industry definitions and exclusions
sources.summary: Official establishment classifications support business-role and detailed-industry exception review; they do not establish accounting treatments.

sources.title: IFRS 13: public scope and fair-value overview
sources.summary: The publisher explains that IFRS 13 supplies a measurement framework when another standard calls for fair value. The entity intention to hold an asset does not determine the market-participant exit price.

sources.title: Holdings of cryptocurrencies: final June 2019 IFRIC agenda decision
sources.summary: For the described cryptocurrency subset, the Committee concluded that IAS 2 applies when held for sale in the ordinary course of business; otherwise IAS 38 applies. The decision explains why those facts do not meet cash or financial-asset definitions.

sources.title: GASB 34: governmental funds and government-wide reconciliation
sources.summary: Selected operative paragraphs distinguish the governmental-fund measurement basis from government-wide accrual reporting and require reconciliations for capital assets, long-term obligations and other differences.

sources.title: GASB 103: reporting model changes and budget comparison requirements
sources.summary: The selected amendments require budget comparison information in required supplementary information, with original-to-final and final-to-actual variances, and apply for fiscal years beginning after June 15, 2025.

sources.title: SFFAS 34: federal GAAP hierarchy and limited FASB reporting exceptions
sources.summary: The standard orders sources of federal accounting guidance, addresses missing guidance and retains limited circumstances in which a federal entity reports under FASB standards.

sources.title: SFFAS 53: budget and accrual reconciliation for federal component entities
sources.summary: The budget and accrual reconciliation starts with net cost and explains adjustments to net outlays, including depreciation, capital acquisitions and timing differences. It distinguishes component reporting from the consolidated US government report.

sources.title: IAS 32 Financial Instruments: Presentation
sources.summary: Official IFRS Foundation page was opened and the standard scope and recognition or classification summary were read.

sources.title: SEC Rule 206(4)-2 Custody of Funds or Securities of Clients by Investment Advisers
sources.summary: SEC rule text defines custody as holding or authority to obtain possession of client funds or securities and requires qualified-custodian maintenance under specified conditions.

sources.title: 42 CFR 413.24 adequate cost data and cost finding
sources.summary: The current eCFR requires providers receiving payment on a reimbursable-cost basis to provide adequate cost data based on financial and statistical records verifiable by qualified auditors; defines cost finding as recasting account data through direct allocation and indirect proration; and requires adequate data from provider records. Paragraph (f)(2)(i) sets the due date at the last day of the fifth month after the covered period (or 150 days when the period ends other than month-end); (f)(2)(ii) limits contractor extensions to operations significantly adversely affected by extraordinary circumstances beyond the provider’s control. The rule lists post-period cost-finding methods and exceptions, so a claims or encounter population cannot simply be treated as the cost ledger.
sources.publisher: Office of the Federal Register; HHS

sources.title: CMS Provider Reimbursement Manual 2552-10 hospital cost report instructions
sources.summary: The CMS 2552-10 instructions state that filing is mandatory, identify the form as effective for hospitals and hospital health care complexes with periods beginning on or after May 1, 2010, and use the certification requiring the report and balance sheet/statement of revenues and expenses to be true, correct, complete and prepared from provider books and records. The Worksheet S-2 Part I identifies the provider CCN, component provider types, payment system columns and cost-reporting period, showing why entity/component and period fields are required before reconciling populations.

sources.title: FASB ASU 2018-08: contributions, exchange transactions and conditions
sources.summary: FASB amendment distinguishes reciprocal exchange transactions from contributions and makes a contribution conditional only when an agreement includes both a barrier and a right of return or release.

sources.title: FASB ASU 2016-14: NFP presentation, restrictions and functional expenses
sources.summary: FASB amendment establishes two net-asset classes, donor-restriction release presentation, liquidity disclosures, endowment disclosures and expense reporting by nature and function for not-for-profit entities.

sources.title: IRS 2025 Form 990 instructions: functional expenses and federal reporting
sources.summary: IRS instructions route selected Form 990 schedules from Part IV, define endowment and donated-service reporting boundaries, and require covered exempt organizations to report functional expenses and document reasonable allocation methods; federal tax reporting can differ from financial-statement GAAP.

sources.title: ASU 2016-08: principal-versus-agent presentation
sources.summary: Amends Topic 606 to clarify that principal-versus-agent presentation turns on whether the entity controls a specified good or service before transfer; the current Codification remains authoritative.

sources.title: FASB ASU 2015-02: Consolidation
sources.summary: Official FASB Accounting Standards Update simplifying the US GAAP consolidation analysis around voting-interest and variable-interest models. The retained synthesis is limited to the cited Topic 810 control and transition paragraphs.

sources.title: FERC electric utility Uniform System of Accounts
sources.summary: Part 101 applies to specified Federal Power Act utilities and licensees. Account 182.3 concerns regulatory-created assets arising from ratemaking actions.
sources.publisher: FERC; Office of the Federal Register

sources.title: SEC investment adviser client custody rule
sources.summary: Covered advisers must use qualified custodians, client notices and statements, and independent verification subject to the rule exceptions. Custody and ownership are separate facts.
sources.publisher: SEC; Office of the Federal Register

sources.title: SEC oil and gas accounting method boundaries, 2025 CFR
sources.summary: The successful-efforts route points to ASC 932. Full-cost rules distinguish country cost centers, acquisition/exploration/development capitalization, amortization, ceiling limits and production expense.

sources.title: NAIC statutory accounting and state practice boundaries
sources.summary: The AP&P framework supports insurer statutory reporting; state prescribed and permitted practices can differ. Statutory solvency reporting is a distinct reporting purpose.

sources.title: USDA ARMS documentation: production and farm financial populations
sources.summary: The survey distinguishes acreage, output, commodity contracts, custom work, input spending, assets and debt. Those categories inform evidence intake without supplying entity-level GAAP cost eligibility.

sources.title: FASB Statement 57: related-party disclosure research
sources.summary: Relationships, transactions, balances and settlement terms require distinct evidence. An arm's-length claim needs substantiation; some control relationships matter without transactions.

sources.title: 2025 Instructions for Form 1120, U.S. Corporation Income Tax Return
sources.summary: Current IRS instructions for a 2025 Form 1120 return, including who must file, the period covered, signature and filing mechanics, and Schedule M-1 or M-3 book-to-tax reconciliation context.

sources.title: FASB ASU 2016-01: Recognition and Measurement of Financial Assets and Financial Liabilities
sources.summary: The Update generally measures equity investments within its scope at fair value through net income and provides a measurement alternative for equity securities without readily determinable fair value, subject to the stated impairment and observable-price-change requirements.

sources.title: FASB ASU 2016-13: Measurement of Credit Losses on Financial Instruments
sources.summary: The Update replaces the incurred-loss model with an expected-credit-loss model for financial assets within its scope and requires reasonable and supportable information without prescribing one estimation method.

sources.title: FASB ASU 2022-03: Fair Value Measurement of Equity Securities Subject to Contractual Sale Restrictions
sources.summary: The Update clarifies that a contractual sale restriction is not separately recognized and does not automatically produce a discount in fair value, while adding disclosure requirements for qualifying equity securities.

sources.title: FASB Accounting Standards Codification Topic 820: Fair Value Measurement locator
sources.summary: The locator identifies the authorized US GAAP fair-value paragraphs needed to connect unit of account, market-participant assumptions, observability and disclosure evidence.

sources.title: FASB Accounting Standards Codification Topic 360: Long-Lived Asset Impairment locator
sources.summary: The locator identifies the authorized US GAAP impairment paragraphs for determining scope, triggering events, recoverability and measurement of long-lived assets.

sources.title: FASB ASU 2025-02: Liabilities (Topic 405), Amendments to SEC Paragraphs Pursuant to SEC Staff Accounting Bulletin No. 122
sources.summary: The Update aligns the Codification with the rescission of SAB Topic 5.FF by removing the former safeguarding reference. It is a later Codification alignment point, not a conclusion that all custody arrangements are off balance sheet.

sources.title: FASB ASU 2019-10: Financial Instruments Credit Losses, Derivatives and Hedging, and Leases, Effective Dates
sources.summary: This amendment defers selected credit-loss and nonpublic hedging adoption dates. Classify the reporting entity and preserve evidence of any early adoption.

sources.title: Illinois Uniform Prudent Management of Institutional Funds Act, 760 ILCS 51
sources.summary: Selected Illinois institutional-fund provisions provide a state-law routing example for donor instruments, prudent endowment management, modification of restrictions and no-hindsight review; they are not a national nonprofit endowment rule.

sources.title: ARB 51 as amended by FAS 160: historical consolidation procedures
sources.summary: Historical amended consolidation procedures identify the group as one economic entity and address intercompany balances, transactions and parent-company presentation.
sources.publisher: AICPA Committee on Accounting Procedure; amended text hosted by FASB

sources.title: OCC allowances for credit losses and CECL process guidance
sources.summary: OCC describes expected credit loss measurement, impairment of available-for-sale debt securities, estimation controls, management responsibility and examiner review for bank accounting.
sources.publisher: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency

sources.title: SEC good-faith fair-value determinations under Rule 2a-5
sources.summary: SEC Rule 2a-5 provides a framework for registered investment companies and business development companies to determine fair value in good faith, including board or valuation-designee oversight, valuation risks, methodologies and records.

sources.title: SEC broker-dealer customer protection rule locator
sources.summary: The customer protection rule requires covered broker-dealers to safeguard customer cash and securities through possession or control and reserve computations, with scope and compliance dates depending on the rule and firm.
sources.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission; Office of the Federal Register

sources.title: NAIC 2026 Accounting Practices and Procedures Manual
sources.summary: The NAIC AP&P Manual contains statutory accounting guidance adopted through March 2026, including SSAP material, cross-reference and implementation material; state prescribed or permitted practices remain separate.

sources.title: IRS exempt-organization gaming and unrelated business taxable income
sources.summary: IRS guidance routes exempt-organization gaming through unrelated-business-income factors and exceptions, including bingo, volunteer labor, public entertainment and member or nonmember distinctions. It also calls for separate gross gaming receipts and prize/disbursement records.

sources.title: FTC Funeral Rule: pre-need and at-need consumer disclosures
sources.summary: Federal consumer-protection guidance applies the Funeral Rule to pre-need and at-need arrangements, price lists and selected goods/services choices. It supplies contract and control inputs, not a GAAP recognition conclusion.

sources.title: IRS Publication 926: household employer tax route
sources.summary: IRS household-employer guidance helps determine whether a household worker is an employee and whether federal Social Security, Medicare, FUTA or withholding obligations and Schedule H reporting apply.

sources.title: SEC Family Offices final rule, published 2011
sources.summary: The published rule excludes qualifying family offices from the Advisers Act investment-adviser definition using client, ownership/control and public-holding-out conditions. Its multifamily discussion does not extend that exclusion to offices serving multiple families.

sources.title: Texas Property Code Chapter 116: selected principal and income provisions
sources.summary: The selected provisions prioritize the governing instrument, separate specified principal and income receipts, and split accounting expenses involving both income and remainder interests. The allocation rules do not determine federal taxable income.
sources.source_type: Texas fiduciary principal and income law

sources.title: IRS 2025 partner instructions for Schedule K-1 (Form 1065)
sources.summary: Partner reporting can arise without a cash distribution. The partner must maintain adjusted outside basis; a K-1 capital account is not automatically that basis.

sources.title: IRS 2025 Form 1041 instructions for estates and trusts
sources.summary: Fiduciary accounting income under the instrument and local law enters a separate federal calculation. Schedule B and DNI help determine the distribution deduction and beneficiary reporting; cash paid alone does not settle tax character.
sources.source_type: US federal fiduciary income tax guidance

sources.title: IRS 2025 beneficiary instructions for Schedule K-1 (Form 1041)
sources.summary: A beneficiary uses the fiduciary K-1 to report the assigned tax items on the individual return. Errors require the fiduciary correction or inconsistent-treatment route, rather than silently changing the received K-1.

sources.title: IRS Publication 559 (2025): survivor, executor and administrator reporting routes
sources.summary: A decedent’s final individual income return, the estate’s income return and estate/gift transfer-tax information have different taxpayers and purposes. The publication routes estate and gift questions to Forms 706 and 709 and their instructions without supplying all exceptions.
sources.source_type: US federal estate and gift tax guidance

Nacha fraud-monitoring material remains network-specific and is not generalized to assurance work.

questions.question: How should a selected federal component entity separate appropriation authority, net cost, net outlays and federal-award controls?
questions.scope: A US federal component reporting entity with an illustrative appropriation, grant and budget/accrual reconciliation; not the consolidated US Government and not a spending-authority conclusion.
questions.answer: SFFAS 34 directs a federal reporting entity through the FASAB hierarchy and preserves limited, fact-specific FASB reporting circumstances. SFFAS 53 requires a component-entity budget and accrual reconciliation using net cost, noncash costs, capital acquisitions and timing differences. The Green Book supplies a federal internal-control reference, while 2 CFR Part 200 governs only the selected federal-award branch. None of these selected sources authorizes an appropriation or proves a live agency balance.

questions.question: How should a household employer control reimbursements and household asset custody alongside payroll?
questions.scope: Selected US other-services residual branches in NAICS 811, 812, 813 and 814; illustrative 2026 close. US GAAP, federal tax and consumer-protection routes remain separate. No whole-subsector sufficiency is asserted.
questions.answer: Keep household asset purchases and authorized reimbursements outside wage expense unless the facts make them compensation, retain receipts and approvals, and track worker-held supplies as custody rather than business inventory.

sources.title: AS 1105, Audit Evidence
sources.summary: Governs the sufficiency, appropriateness, and reliability of information an agent retrieves, transforms, or helps evaluate.

sources.title: AS 2110, Identifying and Assessing Risks of Material Misstatement
sources.summary: Requires an understanding of information systems and controls, including AI-enabled processes that create or alter financial information.

sources.title: AS 2201, An Audit of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting
sources.summary: Core requirements for evaluating whether an agent workflow introduces, changes, or depends on key ICFR controls.

sources.title: AS 2401, Consideration of Fraud in a Financial Statement Audit
sources.summary: Relevant to AI-assisted fraud work and to manipulation, fabricated evidence, and management-override risks.

sources.title: QC 1000, A Firm's System of Quality Control
sources.summary: Issued and SEC-approved but not yet effective at the review date. Covers technological resources, providers, monitoring, remediation, and accountability.

sources.title: Statements on Auditing Standards: Currently Effective
sources.summary: The authoritative AU-C baseline for responsibilities, evidence, documentation, risk, service organizations, estimates, and specialists.

sources.title: SAS No. 145, Understanding the Entity and Assessing Risks of Material Misstatement
sources.summary: Requires understanding IT, information processing, and controls that form the risk-assessment base for agent-enabled systems.

sources.title: Using Artificial Intelligence for Fraud Risk Assessment
sources.summary: Compares novice and experienced auditors using AI in a fraud-risk task. Results remain specific to the task, model, and materials.

sources.title: AuditFraudBench: Benchmarking Audit Judgment in Fraudulent Misstatements
sources.summary: Tests numeric and narrative reasoning against original and restated filings and SEC enforcement releases. It is retrospective, not a live detector.

sources.title: Standards for Internal Control in the Federal Government, 2025 Green Book
sources.summary: Current federal internal-control standard covering authority, risk, control activities, information, monitoring, fraud, and remediation. Outside federal scope, use it as guidance rather than binding law.

sources.title: Risk Management Topics — Fraud Monitoring, Phase 2
sources.summary: Risk-based ACH fraud-monitoring requirements for in-scope participants, including false-pretenses fraud. Do not apply the rule to unrelated payment rails or roles.

sources.title: Advisory FIN-2016-A003 on Business Email Compromise
sources.summary: Official advisory describing changed-payment-instruction fraud and verification patterns. It supports a control pattern but is not a universal legal mandate for every organization.

sources.title: Internal Audit and AI-Enabled Fraud
sources.summary: A survey of 373 senior internal-audit leaders covers AI-enabled fraud risk, readiness, and internal-audit use. Vendor partnership, regional selection, and self-report mean preparedness perceptions are not fraud-detection performance.
sources.publisher: Internal Audit Foundation and The Institute of Internal Auditors with AuditBoard

sources.title: Strengthening standards for software that integrates with HMRC
sources.summary: A proposed direction covers product integrity, correct outcomes, data accountability, error handling, and prevention of fraud and misuse. Detailed standards remain under development during 2026–27, so the record is not final technical requirements.

sources.title: The Financial Stability Implications of Artificial Intelligence
sources.summary: Identifies third-party concentration, correlated behavior, cyber risk, model risk, data quality, governance, fraud, and disinformation as potential systemic vulnerabilities. It is macroprudential analysis, not entity-level control criteria.

sources.title: Managing Artificial Intelligence-Specific Cybersecurity Risks in the Financial Services Sector
sources.summary: Grounds AI cyber, fraud, data, governance, and third-party recommendations in interviews with 42 financial-services and technology organizations. Interview evidence and recommendations do not create binding requirements.

sources.title: 2 CFR Part 200, Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards
sources.summary: Current eCFR Part 200 requires federal-award costs to be necessary, reasonable, allocable, consistently treated, GAAP-based where applicable, documented, and not double charged; §§200.302, 200.328, 200.329 and 200.501 provide selected financial-management, reporting, performance-monitoring and audit-routing requirements. It is an external federal-award rule, not a general internal management-accounting standard.
sources.publisher: US Office of Management and Budget and eCFR

sources.title: AuditAgent: Expert-Guided Multi-Agent Reasoning for Cross-Document Fraudulent Evidence Discovery
sources.summary: AuditAgent studies evidence-chain localization across reports in documented financial-fraud cases.

sources.title: EDINET-Bench: Evaluating LLMs on Complex Financial Tasks using Japanese Financial Statements
sources.summary: Japanese annual-report tasks test fraud detection, earnings forecasting and industry prediction.
sources.publisher: Sugiura and coauthors; Sakana AI / ICLR 2026

sources.title: Bank Account Fraud Dataset Suite — NeurIPS 2022
sources.summary: Six synthetic bank-application datasets expose imbalance, bias and temporal shifts.

sources.title: Financial Fraud Alert Review Dataset — 2025 release
sources.summary: FiFAR pairs high-risk bank-application instances with simulated reviewer decisions.
sources.publisher: Alves and coauthors; Springer Nature Figshare

sources.summary: The standard orders sources of federal accounting guidance, addresses missing guidance and retains limited circumstances in which a federal entity reports under FASB standards.

sources.summary: The budget and accrual reconciliation starts with net cost and explains adjustments to net outlays, including depreciation, capital acquisitions and timing differences. It distinguishes component reporting from the consolidated US government report.

sources.summary: The decision concerned a November 2022 bereavement-fare chatbot interaction. The chatbot told the customer a fare could be claimed retroactively; Air Canada’s policy contradicted that advice. The tribunal mostly allowed the claim and ordered damages and fees.

sources.title: IRS Publication 926: household employer tax route
sources.summary: IRS household-employer guidance helps determine whether a household worker is an employee and whether federal Social Security, Medicare, FUTA or withholding obligations and Schedule H reporting apply.

questions.answer: For the stated Texas trust, first check the instrument and any authorized adjustment. Selected interest is income; the specified long-held bond-sale proceeds belong to principal. An accounting expense involving both income and remainder interests is split equally under the selected default provisions. The example pays an authorized income distribution and retains income separately. These fiduciary classifications do not determine GAAP presentation, DNI, the distribution deduction or beneficiary tax character.

sources.title: FRS 102 (2024 Edition) Section 1 scope and basis of preparation
sources.summary: Section1.3 requires adoptedIFRS consolidated accounts when law requires them. sources.title: FASB Accounting Standards Codification
sources.summary: The authoritative US GAAP source. Agent-produced accounting remains subject to the same recognition, measurement, presentation, and disclosure requirements.

sources.title: Next-Gen Controllership: Harnessing AI and Emerging Technologies to Transform Finance and Accounting
sources.summary: A survey of more than 900 respondents on controllership technology, barriers, skills, and operating priorities. Results are self-reported, and one coauthor has a commercial transformation practice.
sources.publisher: Institute of Management Accountants and Deloitte

sources.title: Basis scales accounting with trusted agents
sources.summary: Reconciliation, journal-entry, and variance-summary agents with routing, validation, reviewability, and approval. Time-savings claims lack an independent method.

sources.title: IFRS 15, Revenue from Contracts with Customers
sources.summary: Official revenue-recognition anchor. Apply current endorsed text and entity facts; the standard does not grant billing, posting, or approval authority.

sources.title: IAS 2, Inventories
sources.summary: Official inventory-cost, cost-formula, net-realizable-value, and write-down anchor. Physical existence, condition, policy, and current evidence remain fact-specific.

sources.title: The Productivity J-Curve: How Intangibles Complement General Purpose Technologies
sources.summary: Explains why process, software, business-model, and human-capital investments can delay visible productivity from a general-purpose technology. It is not a causal estimate for generative AI or a specific finance deployment.

sources.title: Beyond Accuracy: Behavioral Testing of NLP Models with CheckList
sources.summary: Introduces capability-by-test matrices and invariance, directional, and minimum-functionality tests. It targets NLP classifiers rather than stateful agents, and accounting experts still must define valid behaviors and oracles.

sources.title: Close Automation — General Availability
sources.summary: Documents close-task monitoring, subledger-to-general-ledger reconciliation assistance, variance alerts, permissions, dependencies, and regional availability. It establishes documented product behavior, not autonomous accounting or independently measured outcomes.

sources.title: Staff Accounting Bulletin No. 99 — Materiality
sources.summary: SEC Staff Accounting Bulletin No. 99 says exclusive reliance on a numerical materiality threshold is inappropriate and that qualitative context, aggregation, trends, incentives, covenants, and the effect on users can matter. It is SEC staff guidance for registrants, not a Commission rule or a general internal performance-metric standard.
sources.publisher: US Securities and Exchange Commission staff

sources.title: ASU 2018-15: Customer's Accounting for Implementation Costs in a Cloud Computing Arrangement
sources.summary: Addresses capitalization, expense, amortization, impairment, and presentation of implementation costs in service-contract cloud arrangements. The issued update is not a substitute for the current Codification or a fact-specific conclusion.

sources.title: Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 Manufacturing Profile
sources.summary: Maps CSF 2.0 governance and cybersecurity outcomes to manufacturing environments, including supply-chain, platform, and infrastructure resilience. It remains a closed-comment draft, voluntary, and cyber-focused rather than accounting-specific.
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology

sources.title: 2 CFR Part 200, Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards
sources.summary: Current eCFR Part 200 requires federal-award costs to be necessary, reasonable, allocable, consistently treated, GAAP-based where applicable, documented, and not double charged; §§200.302, 200.328, 200.329 and 200.501 provide selected financial-management, reporting, performance-monitoring and audit-routing requirements. It is an external federal-award rule, not a general internal management-accounting standard.
sources.publisher: US Office of Management and Budget and eCFR

sources.title: Publication 15 (2026), Circular E, Employer’s Tax Guide
sources.summary: The annual employer guide provides the federal payroll-tax context for withholding, deposits, reporting, and recordkeeping.

sources.title: Running payroll: Reporting to HMRC — Full Payment Submission
sources.summary: HMRC explains Full Payment Submission timing, payment-date reporting, corrections, and the employee information reported through payroll software.

sources.title: CMS HCRIS provider cost-report data
sources.summary: Public Medicare provider cost reports contain utilization, cost-center, settlement and financial-statement data.

sources.title: ASU 2014-09: original revenue recognition amendments, Section A
sources.summary: Sets out over-time criteria, progress measurement and contract-balance presentation; input measures may require adjustment for costs that do not depict performance.

sources.title: 2022 NAICS United States manual: industry definitions and exclusions
sources.summary: Official establishment classifications support business-role and detailed-industry exception review; they do not establish accounting treatments.

sources.title: IAS 19: public employee-benefit scope and measurement overview
sources.summary: The publisher separates short-term benefits, fixed-contribution plans without further obligation, defined-benefit measurement and the trigger for termination benefits.

sources.title: GASB 103: reporting model changes and budget comparison requirements
sources.summary: The selected amendments require budget comparison information in required supplementary information, with original-to-final and final-to-actual variances, and apply for fiscal years beginning after June 15, 2025.

sources.title: Inventory accounting: IFRS Accounting Standards vs US GAAP
sources.summary: KPMG’s current comparison states that IAS 2 prohibits LIFO, generally uses lower of cost and NRV, and requires reversal of write-downs up to original cost; US GAAP permits LIFO and prohibits reversals, with market measurement for LIFO/retail inventories.

sources.title: FASB ASU 2018-08: contributions, exchange transactions and conditions
sources.summary: FASB amendment distinguishes reciprocal exchange transactions from contributions and makes a contribution conditional only when an agreement includes both a barrier and a right of return or release.

sources.title: FASB ASU 2016-14: NFP presentation, restrictions and functional expenses
sources.summary: FASB amendment establishes two net-asset classes, donor-restriction release presentation, liquidity disclosures, endowment disclosures and expense reporting by nature and function for not-for-profit entities.

sources.title: IRS 2025 Form 990 instructions: functional expenses and federal reporting
sources.summary: IRS instructions route selected Form 990 schedules from Part IV, define endowment and donated-service reporting boundaries, and require covered exempt organizations to report functional expenses and document reasonable allocation methods; federal tax reporting can differ from financial-statement GAAP.

sources.title: ASU 2016-08: principal-versus-agent presentation
sources.summary: Amends Topic 606 to clarify that principal-versus-agent presentation turns on whether the entity controls a specified good or service before transfer; the current Codification remains authoritative.

sources.title: ASU 2015-11: inventory measured at lower of cost and net realizable value
sources.summary: Amends Topic 330 so inventory measured by methods other than LIFO or the retail method, including FIFO or average cost, is subsequently measured at the lower of cost and net realizable value; scope and transition are explicit.

sources.title: FASB December 18, 2024 board handout: Topic 330 inventory measurement
sources.summary: A FASB staff board handout describes ASC 330-10-30-1 as using cost as the primary inventory measurement basis and explains that acquisition and production costs bring inventory to its existing condition and location.
sources.source_type: FASB staff board meeting handout; non-authoritative

sources.title: FAR 31.203: Indirect costs
sources.summary: FAR 31.203 requires covered federal contractors to group indirect costs logically, select a common base based on benefits to cost objectives, avoid inconsistent direct and indirect treatment, and revise methods when business circumstances materially change. It applies to covered federal contracts, not ordinary internal management reporting.

sources.title: RMA Common Crop Insurance Policy Basic Provisions 26-BR
sources.summary: Production and acreage reports identify shares, units, gross/net output and deductions. Loss notices and supporting production evidence are separate from sale records and ledger recognition.

sources.title: NOAA commercial fisheries landings: quantity and value documentation
sources.summary: Landing populations use dealer/fisher records including trip tickets. Landed quantity and value are evidence categories; they do not establish inventory valuation or ownership of uncaught fish.

sources.title: NOAA Catch Shares: allocation and program boundaries
sources.summary: Catch-share arrangements allocate allowable catch. The accounting for an acquired quota/access right requires its own legal and measurement analysis.

sources.title: USDA ARMS documentation: production and farm financial populations
sources.summary: The survey distinguishes acreage, output, commodity contracts, custom work, input spending, assets and debt. Those categories inform evidence intake without supplying entity-level GAAP cost eligibility.

sources.title: FASB Statement 57: related-party disclosure research

questions.question: Which family office taxpayer and year should receive K-1, basis and estate/gift information?
questions.scope: US office service company, domestic investment LLC taxed as a partnership, Texas domestic non-grantor complex trust, and individual; synthetic September 2026 close. Tax coordination uses explicitly selected 2025 IRS instructions as prior-year routing, not 2026 return instructions.
questions.answer: Use separate taxpayer and tax-year identifiers. The investment partnership issues partner K-1 information; the individual and trust receive their own shares, including income not distributed. Maintain outside basis independently from K-1 capital. The non-grantor trust uses the fiduciary return and beneficiary K-1 route, while the individual uses the individual return and the assumed office C corporation retains its corporate route. Collect donor, donee, transfer-date/value and prior-gift evidence for gift-tax review, and decedent, death-date, ownership/value and prior-transfer evidence for estate review. No filing requirement, tax amount or planning action is determined.

questions.question: How can a family office reconcile a supplemental family statement without double counting?
questions.scope: US office service company, domestic investment LLC taxed as a partnership, Texas domestic non-grantor complex trust, and individual; synthetic September 2026 close. Tax coordination uses explicitly selected 2025 IRS instructions as prior-year routing, not 2026 return instructions.
questions.answer: Complete separate bank, custodian and ledger reconciliations, then define the included accounts and purpose of a supplemental view. Remove duplicated interests only where the underlying entity is also included, match interentity balances, and distinguish internal fees and beneficiary transfers from external activity. Retain the entity trial balances and an adjustment log. The original four-entity example shows a balanced carrying-value aggregation, including restricted trust resources and an unresolved valuation exception; it is not an individual’s net worth or a final GAAP financial statement. Payment-authority and sensitive-data controls are editorial proposals.

sources.title: FASB Accounting Standards Codification
sources.summary: The authoritative US GAAP source. Agent-produced accounting remains subject to the same recognition, measurement, presentation, and disclosure requirements.

sources.title: IFRS 9, Financial Instruments
sources.summary: Official anchor for classification, measurement, expected credit losses, and hedge accounting. Current endorsed text, instrument facts, and approved judgments control.

sources.title: IFRS 10, Consolidated Financial Statements
sources.summary: Official consolidation anchor built around control. Verify the current entity perimeter, ownership facts, amendments, and local endorsement before applying it.

sources.title: Publication 15 (2026), Circular E, Employer’s Tax Guide
sources.summary: The annual employer guide provides the federal payroll-tax context for withholding, deposits, reporting, and recordkeeping.

sources.title: FFIEC 051 Call Report instructions — December 2025
sources.summary: Quarterly bank-reporting instructions define eligibility, report schedules and accounting glossary context.

sources.title: OCC Bank Accounting Advisory Series — 2026
sources.summary: OCC staff interpretations address banking accounting fact patterns and regulatory-reporting questions.
sources.publisher: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency

sources.title: NAIC statutory accounting hierarchy and AP&P Manual
sources.summary: NAIC describes the authority hierarchy behind insurer statutory financial reporting.

sources.title: ASU 2014-09: original revenue recognition amendments, Section A
sources.summary: Sets out over-time criteria, progress measurement and contract-balance presentation; input measures may require adjustment for costs that do not depict performance.

sources.title: Texas Property Code Chapter 162: construction trust funds
sources.summary: Provides statutory trust-fund duties for covered construction payments and distinct residential account requirements.

sources.title: Texas Property Code Chapter 53: mechanic’s and materialman’s liens
sources.summary: Provides a Texas statutory framework for construction lien rights, notices, retained funds and waivers.

sources.title: ASU 2025-05: credit losses for current receivables and contract assets
sources.summary: Provides a practical expedient for all entities and a subsequent-collection policy election for entities other than public business entities, for eligible current ASC 606 receivables and contract assets.

sources.title: ASU 2018-17: common-control consolidation alternative
sources.summary: Allows qualifying private companies to elect an alternative to VIE analysis for qualifying common-control entities, while other consolidation guidance and disclosures remain applicable.

sources.title: 2022 NAICS United States manual: industry definitions and exclusions
sources.summary: Official establishment classifications support business-role and detailed-industry exception review; they do not establish accounting treatments.

sources.title: GASB 34: governmental funds and government-wide reconciliation
sources.summary: Selected operative paragraphs distinguish the governmental-fund measurement basis from government-wide accrual reporting and require reconciliations for capital assets, long-term obligations and other differences.

sources.title: GASB 103: reporting model changes and budget comparison requirements
sources.summary: The selected amendments require budget comparison information in required supplementary information, with original-to-final and final-to-actual variances, and apply for fiscal years beginning after June 15, 2025.

sources.title: Texas annual financial reporting instructions: modified accrual overview
sources.summary: The current Texas reporting instructions explain why governmental funds exclude general capital assets and depreciation while government-wide reporting includes the noncurrent activity.

sources.title: IAS 32 Financial Instruments: Presentation
sources.summary: Official IFRS Foundation page was opened and the standard scope and recognition or classification summary were read.

sources.title: SEC Rule 206(4)-2 Custody of Funds or Securities of Clients by Investment Advisers
sources.summary: SEC rule text defines custody as holding or authority to obtain possession of client funds or securities and requires qualified-custodian maintenance under specified conditions.

sources.title: FASB ASU 2016-14: NFP presentation, restrictions and functional expenses
sources.summary: FASB amendment establishes two net-asset classes, donor-restriction release presentation, liquidity disclosures, endowment disclosures and expense reporting by nature and function for not-for-profit entities.

sources.title: IRS 2025 Form 990 instructions: functional expenses and federal reporting
sources.summary: IRS instructions route selected Form 990 schedules from Part IV, define endowment and donated-service reporting boundaries, and require covered exempt organizations to report functional expenses and document reasonable allocation methods; federal tax reporting can differ from financial-statement GAAP.

sources.title: ASU 2016-08: principal-versus-agent presentation
sources.summary: Amends Topic 606 to clarify that principal-versus-agent presentation turns on whether the entity controls a specified good or service before transfer; the current Codification remains authoritative.

sources.title: ASU 2016-13: current expected credit losses
sources.summary: Amends Topic 326 to require an allowance for expected credit losses using relevant past events, current conditions and reasonable and supportable forecasts, with reporting-date updates to the allowance.

sources.title: FASB ASU 2015-02: Consolidation
sources.summary: Official FASB Accounting Standards Update simplifying the US GAAP consolidation analysis around voting-interest and variable-interest models. The retained synthesis is limited to the cited Topic 810 control and transition paragraphs.

sources.title: FSA Handbook 2025-2026: Disbursing Title IV funds
sources.summary: Program administration for eligible institutions, not accounting recognition authority.

sources.title: FSA Handbook 2025-2026: Withdrawal and return of Title IV funds
sources.summary: The 2025-2026 program-year guidance is not a determination of later July2026 rule applicability.

sources.title: GASB Statement 35: Public colleges and universities
sources.summary: Original November1999 statement, not current consolidated GASB guidance; later amendments require separate review.

sources.title: SEC investment adviser client custody rule
sources.summary: Covered advisers must use qualified custodians, client notices and statements, and independent verification subject to the rule exceptions. Custody and ownership are separate facts.
sources.publisher: SEC; Office of the Federal Register

sources.title: NAIC statutory accounting and state practice boundaries
sources.summary: The AP&P framework supports insurer statutory reporting; state prescribed and permitted practices can differ. Statutory solvency reporting is a distinct reporting purpose.

sources.title: FASB Statement 57: related-party disclosure research
sources.summary: Relationships, transactions, balances and settlement terms require distinct evidence. An arm's-length claim needs substantiation; some control relationships matter without transactions.

sources.title: 2025 Instructions for Form 1120, U.S. Corporation Income Tax Return
sources.summary: Current IRS instructions for a 2025 Form 1120 return, including who must file, the period covered, signature and filing mechanics, and Schedule M-1 or M-3 book-to-tax reconciliation context.

sources.title: FASB ASU 2016-01: Recognition and Measurement of Financial Assets and Financial Liabilities
sources.summary: The Update generally measures equity investments within its scope at fair value through net income and provides a measurement alternative for equity securities without readily determinable fair value, subject to the stated impairment and observable-price-change requirements.

sources.title: FASB ASU 2016-13: Measurement of Credit Losses on Financial Instruments
sources.summary: The Update replaces the incurred-loss model with an expected-credit-loss model for financial assets within its scope and requires reasonable and supportable information without prescribing one estimation method.

sources.title: FASB ASU 2022-03: Fair Value Measurement of Equity Securities Subject to Contractual Sale Restrictions
sources.summary: The Update clarifies that a contractual sale restriction is not separately recognized and does not automatically produce a discount in fair value, while adding disclosure requirements for qualifying equity securities.

sources.title: FASB Accounting Standards Codification Topic 820: Fair Value Measurement locator
sources.summary: The locator identifies the authorized US GAAP fair-value paragraphs needed to connect unit of account, market-participant assumptions, observability and disclosure evidence.

sources.title: FASB ASU 2019-10: Financial Instruments Credit Losses, Derivatives and Hedging, and Leases, Effective Dates
sources.summary: This amendment defers selected credit-loss and nonpublic hedging adoption dates. Classify the reporting entity and preserve evidence of any early adoption.

sources.title: DOL Fact Sheet 21: Recordkeeping Requirements under the Fair Labor Standards Act
sources.summary: The DOL fact sheet summarizes federal FLSA payroll and timekeeping records, retention periods and the nonbinding relationship to the underlying regulation. It is a labor-evidence source, not a GAAP conclusion.
sources.publisher: United States Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division

sources.title: 49 CFR Part 374, regular-route passenger ticketing and service
sources.summary: For the selected regular-route passenger role, schedules and ticket/refund terms supply evidence distinct from freight billing. Unused-ticket refunds follow the governing tariff; fare receipts alone do not establish accounting recognition.

sources.title: Illinois Uniform Prudent Management of Institutional Funds Act, 760 ILCS 51
sources.summary: Selected Illinois institutional-fund provisions provide a state-law routing example for donor instruments, prudent endowment management, modification of restrictions and no-hindsight review; they are not a national nonprofit endowment rule.

sources.title: ARB 51 as amended by FAS 160: historical consolidation procedures
sources.summary: Historical amended consolidation procedures identify the group as one economic entity and address intercompany balances, transactions and parent-company presentation.
sources.publisher: AICPA Committee on Accounting Procedure; amended text hosted by FASB

sources.title: 2025 Regulation S-X 3A-02: registrant consolidation perimeter
sources.summary: Dated SEC rule describes a registrant consolidation perimeter, with control-based exceptions to ownership heuristics.
sources.publisher: Securities and Exchange Commission via GovInfo

sources.title: OCC allowances for credit losses and CECL process guidance
sources.summary: OCC describes expected credit loss measurement, impairment of available-for-sale debt securities, estimation controls, management responsibility and examiner review for bank accounting.
sources.publisher: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency

sources.title: SEC good-faith fair-value determinations under Rule 2a-5
sources.summary: SEC Rule 2a-5 provides a framework for registered investment companies and business development companies to determine fair value in good faith, including board or valuation-designee oversight, valuation risks, methodologies and records.

sources.title: SEC broker-dealer customer protection rule locator
sources.summary: The customer protection rule requires covered broker-dealers to safeguard customer cash and securities through possession or control and reserve computations, with scope and compliance dates depending on the rule and firm.
sources.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission; Office of the Federal Register

sources.title: NAIC 2026 Accounting Practices and Procedures Manual
sources.summary: The NAIC AP&P Manual contains statutory accounting guidance adopted through March 2026, including SSAP material, cross-reference and implementation material; state prescribed or permitted practices remain separate.

sources.title: Publication 15-A (2026), Employer’s Supplemental Tax Guide
sources.summary: IRS 15-A supplies federal worker-classification and withholding context: the substance of control, financial factors and relationship matters, and labels alone do not decide employee status.

sources.title: California Rule of Professional Conduct 1.15: Safekeeping Funds and Property of Clients and Other Persons
sources.summary: California Rule 1.15 requires separation, accounting and timely treatment of client or third-party funds in the selected California lawyer route.

sources.title: IRS exempt-organization gaming and unrelated business taxable income
sources.summary: IRS guidance routes exempt-organization gaming through unrelated-business-income factors and exceptions, including bingo, volunteer labor, public entertainment and member or nonmember distinctions. It also calls for separate gross gaming receipts and prize/disbursement records.

sources.title: IRS Publication 926: household employer tax route
sources.summary: IRS household-employer guidance helps determine whether a household worker is an employee and whether federal Social Security, Medicare, FUTA or withholding obligations and Schedule H reporting apply.

sources.title: SEC Family Offices final rule, published 2011
sources.summary: The published rule excludes qualifying family offices from the Advisers Act investment-adviser definition using client, ownership/control and public-holding-out conditions. Its multifamily discussion does not extend that exclusion to offices serving multiple families.

sources.title: Texas Property Code Chapter 116: selected principal and income provisions
sources.summary: The selected provisions prioritize the governing instrument, separate specified principal and income receipts, and split accounting expenses involving both income and remainder interests. The allocation rules do not determine federal taxable income.
sources.source_type: Texas fiduciary principal and income law

sources.title: IRS 2025 partner instructions for Schedule K-1 (Form 1065)
sources.summary: Partner reporting can arise without a cash distribution. The partner must maintain adjusted outside basis; a K-1 capital account is not automatically that basis.

sources.title: IRS 2025 Form 1041 instructions for estates and trusts
sources.summary: Fiduciary accounting income under the instrument and local law enters a separate federal calculation. Schedule B and DNI help determine the distribution deduction and beneficiary reporting; cash paid alone does not settle tax character.
sources.source_type: US federal fiduciary income tax guidance

sources.title: IRS 2025 beneficiary instructions for Schedule K-1 (Form 1041)
sources.summary: A beneficiary uses the fiduciary K-1 to report the assigned tax items on the individual return. Errors require the fiduciary correction or inconsistent-treatment route, rather than silently changing the received K-1.

sources.title: IRS Publication 559 (2025): survivor, executor and administrator reporting routes
sources.summary: A decedent’s final individual income return, the estate’s income return and estate/gift transfer-tax information have different taxpayers and purposes. The publication routes estate and gift questions to Forms 706 and 709 and their instructions without supplying all exceptions.
sources.source_type: US federal estate and gift tax guidance

questions.answer: In the synthetic agency branch, tenant rent collected for the owner is a settlement liability while the manager recognizes only the contractually earned fee, subject to current principal-versus-agent analysis. The owner recognizes the tenant deposit liability and a due-from-manager balance; the manager records a separate agency-custody obligation payable to the owner for the deposit. Preserve owner funds, tenant deposits and manager revenue as separate populations.

questions.treatment: For a synthetic $120,000 collection and 5% fee, reconcile $6,000 manager fee, $114,000 owner settlement liability and any separate $20,000 refundable deposit. The owner and manager custody balances are distinct entity books, not two independent tenant obligations. This is a worked control example, not every manager contract.

Classify service and funds
Reconcile receipts to owner and tenant ledgers
Calculate fee
Approve settlement
controls: Separate owner funds
Receipt-to-bank tie
Fee rate and base approval
Owner remittance and deposit liability reconciliation
exceptions: A manager can control a specified service in some arrangements; a broker commission, owner-operated property and tenant security deposit can route differently. Legal fiduciary and trust rules are outside scope.
