sources.title: FASB Accounting Standards Codification
sources.summary: The authoritative US GAAP source. Agent-produced accounting remains subject to the same recognition, measurement, presentation, and disclosure requirements.

sources.title: Next-Gen Controllership: Harnessing AI and Emerging Technologies to Transform Finance and Accounting
sources.summary: A survey of more than 900 respondents on controllership technology, barriers, skills, and operating priorities. Results are self-reported, and one coauthor has a commercial transformation practice.
sources.publisher: Institute of Management Accountants and Deloitte

sources.title: IFRS 15, Revenue from Contracts with Customers
sources.summary: Official revenue-recognition anchor. Apply current endorsed text and entity facts; the standard does not grant billing, posting, or approval authority.

sources.title: IAS 2, Inventories
sources.summary: Official inventory-cost, cost-formula, net-realizable-value, and write-down anchor. Physical existence, condition, policy, and current evidence remain fact-specific.

sources.title: ASU 2018-15: Customer's Accounting for Implementation Costs in a Cloud Computing Arrangement
sources.summary: Addresses capitalization, expense, amortization, impairment, and presentation of implementation costs in service-contract cloud arrangements. The issued update is not a substitute for the current Codification or a fact-specific conclusion.

sources.title: 2 CFR Part 200, Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards
sources.summary: Current eCFR Part 200 requires federal-award costs to be necessary, reasonable, allocable, consistently treated, GAAP-based where applicable, documented, and not double charged; §§200.302, 200.328, 200.329 and 200.501 provide selected financial-management, reporting, performance-monitoring and audit-routing requirements. It is an external federal-award rule, not a general internal management-accounting standard.
sources.publisher: US Office of Management and Budget and eCFR

sources.title: Publication 15 (2026), Circular E, Employer’s Tax Guide
sources.summary: The annual employer guide provides the federal payroll-tax context for withholding, deposits, reporting, and recordkeeping.

sources.title: CMS HCRIS provider cost-report data
sources.summary: Public Medicare provider cost reports contain utilization, cost-center, settlement and financial-statement data.

sources.title: WIP schedules: blueprints for solid construction accounting
sources.summary: Explains how a contractor WIP schedule brings together contract value, estimated costs, costs incurred, earned revenue and billing.

sources.title: ASU 2014-09: original revenue recognition amendments, Section A
sources.summary: Sets out over-time criteria, progress measurement and contract-balance presentation; input measures may require adjustment for costs that do not depict performance.

sources.title: FAR 52.232-5: payments under fixed-price construction contracts
sources.summary: Specifies evidence and conditions for progress payments, including contractor certification and restrictions on payment for stored materials.

sources.title: FAR 52.232-27: prompt payment for construction contracts
sources.summary: Links federal construction payment timing to proper invoices and includes downstream subcontract payment and interest provisions.

sources.title: DCAA preaward accounting system requirements
sources.summary: Describes accounting-system evidence for segregating direct and indirect costs, reconciling job costs to the ledger and identifying unallowable costs.

sources.title: FAR 31.105: construction and architect-engineer contract costs
sources.summary: Identifies settings where federal construction cost principles apply and addresses construction equipment and other cost treatment.

sources.title: Public Law 119-21 §70430: residential construction tax amendments
sources.summary: Expands the residential construction exception and sets application by contracts entered into in taxable years beginning after July 4, 2025.
sources.publisher: U.S. Congress; U.S. Government Publishing Office

sources.title: Financial reporting developments: revenue from contracts with customers, September 2026
sources.summary: Current technical interpretation used to cross-check selected ASC 606 requirements and distinguish modifications, progress inputs and contract balances.

sources.title: Revenue recognition handbook, December 2025: loss-contract scope
sources.summary: Selected loss-contract chapter distinguishes construction and production contracts from excluded ordinary goods and service arrangements.

sources.title: 2022 NAICS United States manual: industry definitions and exclusions
sources.summary: Official establishment classifications support business-role and detailed-industry exception review; they do not establish accounting treatments.

sources.title: Inventory accounting: IFRS Accounting Standards vs US GAAP
sources.summary: KPMG’s current comparison states that IAS 2 prohibits LIFO, generally uses lower of cost and NRV, and requires reversal of write-downs up to original cost; US GAAP permits LIFO and prohibits reversals, with market measurement for LIFO/retail inventories.

sources.title: 26 USC 460: Special rules for long-term contracts, August 2026 preliminary text
sources.summary: Selected construction exceptions and the 2025 amendment effective-date note, checked against enacted section 70430. The taxable-year cohort and contract category constrain the result.
sources.publisher: US House Office of the Law Revision Counsel

sources.title: FASB staff educational paper: construction retainage presentation
sources.summary: Conditional retainage participates in the net contract position. Unconditional receivables remain separate; one contract does not report both a contract asset and liability.

sources.title: GAO-25-107258: construction estimate and final-cost evidence
sources.summary: GAO examined 252 fixed-price construction subcontracts completed in FY2023. Final costs exceeded initial estimates by $37.5 million; $35.6 million arose after award.

sources.title: ASBCA 51759: same-job billing, retainage and supplier-payment evidence
sources.summary: Published findings connect a construction contract, modifications, invoices and payments to an identified job; the underlying complete ledger and exhibits are not supplied.
sources.publisher: Armed Services Board of Contract Appeals

sources.title: FASB ASU 2018-08: contributions, exchange transactions and conditions
sources.summary: FASB amendment distinguishes reciprocal exchange transactions from contributions and makes a contribution conditional only when an agreement includes both a barrier and a right of return or release.

sources.title: FASB ASU 2016-14: NFP presentation, restrictions and functional expenses
sources.summary: FASB amendment establishes two net-asset classes, donor-restriction release presentation, liquidity disclosures, endowment disclosures and expense reporting by nature and function for not-for-profit entities.

sources.title: IRS 2025 Form 990 instructions: functional expenses and federal reporting
sources.summary: IRS instructions route selected Form 990 schedules from Part IV, define endowment and donated-service reporting boundaries, and require covered exempt organizations to report functional expenses and document reasonable allocation methods; federal tax reporting can differ from financial-statement GAAP.

sources.title: ASU 2016-08: principal-versus-agent presentation
sources.summary: Amends Topic 606 to clarify that principal-versus-agent presentation turns on whether the entity controls a specified good or service before transfer; the current Codification remains authoritative.

sources.title: ASU 2015-11: inventory measured at lower of cost and net realizable value
sources.summary: Amends Topic 330 so inventory measured by methods other than LIFO or the retail method, including FIFO or average cost, is subsequently measured at the lower of cost and net realizable value; scope and transition are explicit.

sources.title: Concepts Statement 8, Chapter 4: elements and accrual accounting
sources.summary: Provides non-authoritative conceptual definitions of liabilities, revenues, expenses and accrual accounting, including the distinction between present obligations and future business risks.

sources.title: FAR 31.203: Indirect costs
sources.summary: FAR 31.203 requires covered federal contractors to group indirect costs logically, select a common base based on benefits to cost objectives, avoid inconsistent direct and indirect treatment, and revise methods when business circumstances materially change. It applies to covered federal contracts, not ordinary internal management reporting.

sources.title: USDA ARMS documentation: production and farm financial populations
sources.summary: The survey distinguishes acreage, output, commodity contracts, custom work, input spending, assets and debt. Those categories inform evidence intake without supplying entity-level GAAP cost eligibility.

sources.title: FASB Statement 57: related-party disclosure research
sources.summary: Relationships, transactions, balances and settlement terms require distinct evidence. An arm's-length claim needs substantiation; some control relationships matter without transactions.

sources.title: FASB Statement 5: loss-contingency research
sources.summary: Accrual depends on a probable incurred loss and reasonable estimation. Possible additional losses have separate disclosure requirements; general business-risk reserves are inappropriate.

sources.title: SEC SAB Topic 5.Y: product and environmental claims
sources.summary: Registrant disclosures address estimation uncertainty, recoverability and carrier solvency. A contested indemnification claim carries a rebuttable presumption against recognizing a recovery asset.
sources.publisher: US Securities and Exchange Commission staff

sources.title: DOL Fact Sheet 21: Recordkeeping Requirements under the Fair Labor Standards Act
sources.summary: The DOL fact sheet summarizes federal FLSA payroll and timekeeping records, retention periods and the nonbinding relationship to the underlying regulation. It is a labor-evidence source, not a GAAP conclusion.
sources.publisher: United States Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division

sources.title: FAS 151: historical US inventory conversion, normal capacity and idle overhead
sources.summary: Original November 2004 amendment supporting the historical US normal-capacity and unallocated-overhead treatment; current Codification verification remains open.

sources.title: ASU 2016-10: Identifying Performance Obligations and Licensing
sources.summary: FASB amendments clarify identifying separate performance obligations and license revenue distinctions under Topic 606, including right-to-use versus right-to-access licenses.

sources.title: ARB 51 as amended by FAS 160: historical consolidation procedures
sources.summary: Historical amended consolidation procedures identify the group as one economic entity and address intercompany balances, transactions and parent-company presentation.
sources.publisher: AICPA Committee on Accounting Procedure; amended text hosted by FASB

sources.title: 2025 controlled-services regulation: allocation, benefit and shareholder activities
sources.summary: Dated federal tax text connects controlled services to a recipient benefit, identifies cost-allocation considerations and distinguishes shareholder or passive association activities.
sources.publisher: Internal Revenue Service and Treasury via GovInfo

sources.title: ASU 2010-23: charity-care cost disclosure
sources.summary: The issued amendment measures charity-care disclosure using direct and indirect costs and separately discloses funding received to support that care.

sources.title: FASB Statement 67: costs and initial rental operations of real estate projects
sources.summary: Historical FASB guidance establishes bounded routes for preacquisition, project, allocation, rent and recoverability costs for real estate projects. It is dated source evidence, not current consolidated GAAP.

sources.summary: IRS 15-A supplies federal worker-classification and withholding context: the substance of control, financial factors and relationship matters, and labels alone do not decide employee status.

questions.question: How should a fixed-fee or time-and-material project connect time, WIP, unbilled revenue and billing?
questions.scope: Selected US professional, scientific and technical service roles under the stated framework and effective period; legal client-fund route is California only when governing law is established.
questions.answer: Use approved time, cost-to-complete and contract-right evidence to select and measure the performance obligation. sources.title: FASB Accounting Standards Codification
sources.summary: The authoritative US GAAP source. Agent-produced accounting remains subject to the same recognition, measurement, presentation, and disclosure requirements.

sources.title: Enterprise Risk Management for Cloud Computing
sources.summary: Addresses hosting, data residency, vendor dependency, resilience, and shared-responsibility risks relevant to agent services.

sources.title: Accelerating the Adoption of Software and AI Agent Identity and Authorization
sources.summary: A draft, not final guidance. It frames identity, delegation, authorization, discovery, auditability, and lifecycle problems for software and AI agents.

sources.title: Secure Software Development Practices for Generative AI and Dual-Use Foundation Models
sources.summary: Extends secure-development practices to model, data, and AI supply chains for teams that build or fine-tune agent systems.

sources.title: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks
sources.summary: Introduces task-completion time horizons and measures success as task length increases. The benchmark is concentrated in software and research, and a 50% horizon is not a production-reliability threshold.

sources.title: IFRS 15, Revenue from Contracts with Customers
sources.summary: Official revenue-recognition anchor. Apply current endorsed text and entity facts; the standard does not grant billing, posting, or approval authority.

sources.title: Use of Electronic Accounting Software Records FAQ
sources.summary: Supports retaining original electronic transaction detail, changes, and cutoff information for examination. It is not a universal record-format or retention rule.

sources.title: Agentic AI Foundation projects and working groups
sources.summary: The official foundation site separates hosted projects, focused working groups, governance, current material, and participation routes. It is useful for ecosystem orientation and information architecture; foundation participation or project hosting does not establish accounting suitability, security, or control effectiveness.

sources.title: TheAgentCompany: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Consequential Real World Tasks
sources.summary: Tests sustained work across web, code, office tools, communication, administration, and some finance tasks. The simulated small software company and benchmark-specific graders do not establish accounting deployment reliability.

sources.title: The Productivity J-Curve: How Intangibles Complement General Purpose Technologies
sources.summary: Explains why process, software, business-model, and human-capital investments can delay visible productivity from a general-purpose technology. It is not a causal estimate for generative AI or a specific finance deployment.

sources.title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
sources.summary: An empirical taxonomy covers specification, inter-agent alignment, verification, and termination failures across multi-agent systems. It remains a preprint based on software, math, and general frameworks rather than accounting workflows.

sources.title: Guidelines for using generative artificial intelligence if you're a software developer
sources.summary: Sets expectations for transparent AI use, reliable legal sources, version control, monitoring, human oversight, privacy, security, and ethical design in tax software. It is neither certification nor a replacement for law and filing specifications.

sources.title: Strengthening standards for software that integrates with HMRC
sources.summary: A proposed direction covers product integrity, correct outcomes, data accountability, error handling, and prevention of fraud and misuse. Detailed standards remain under development during 2026–27, so the record is not final technical requirements.

sources.title: Chat BDO's Journey from Pilot to Production
sources.summary: A reported implementation account covering secure hosting, internal knowledge retrieval, personas, adoption, and workflow integration. The article is descriptive, relies on firm interviews, and does not independently validate business outcomes.

sources.title: ASU 2018-15: Customer's Accounting for Implementation Costs in a Cloud Computing Arrangement
sources.summary: Addresses capitalization, expense, amortization, impairment, and presentation of implementation costs in service-contract cloud arrangements. The issued update is not a substitute for the current Codification or a fact-specific conclusion.

sources.title: Accounting Matters
sources.summary: Indexes FERC Uniform Systems of Accounts, forms, orders, and Chief Accountant guidance for electric, gas, and oil-pipeline entities. These regulatory requirements are industry-specific and do not establish an AI-agent design.

sources.title: Initial Risk Assessment on Artificial Intelligence for Critical Energy Infrastructure
sources.summary: Maps AI applications to unintentional failure, adversarial attack, hostile use, and software-supply-chain risks in energy systems. It is an interim operational-risk assessment, not accounting guidance or proof of agent performance.

sources.title: 2 CFR Part 200, Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards
sources.summary: Current eCFR Part 200 requires federal-award costs to be necessary, reasonable, allocable, consistently treated, GAAP-based where applicable, documented, and not double charged; §§200.302, 200.328, 200.329 and 200.501 provide selected financial-management, reporting, performance-monitoring and audit-routing requirements. It is an external federal-award rule, not a general internal management-accounting standard.
sources.publisher: US Office of Management and Budget and eCFR

sources.title: GASB Statement No. 96, Subscription-Based Information Technology Arrangements
sources.summary: Addresses subscription liabilities and assets, implementation stages, capitalization, amortization, and disclosures for government SBITAs. It is public-sector accounting authority, not AI guidance.

sources.title: Publication 15 (2026), Circular E, Employer’s Tax Guide
sources.summary: The annual employer guide provides the federal payroll-tax context for withholding, deposits, reporting, and recordkeeping.

sources.title: Running payroll: Reporting to HMRC — Full Payment Submission
sources.summary: HMRC explains Full Payment Submission timing, payment-date reporting, corrections, and the employee information reported through payroll software.

sources.title: WIP schedules: blueprints for solid construction accounting
sources.summary: Explains how a contractor WIP schedule brings together contract value, estimated costs, costs incurred, earned revenue and billing.

sources.title: ASU 2014-09: original revenue recognition amendments, Section A
sources.summary: Sets out over-time criteria, progress measurement and contract-balance presentation; input measures may require adjustment for costs that do not depict performance.

sources.title: Financial reporting developments: revenue from contracts with customers, September 2026
sources.summary: Current technical interpretation used to cross-check selected ASC 606 requirements and distinguish modifications, progress inputs and contract balances.

sources.title: Revenue recognition handbook, December 2025: loss-contract scope
sources.summary: Selected loss-contract chapter distinguishes construction and production contracts from excluded ordinary goods and service arrangements.

sources.title: 2022 NAICS United States manual: industry definitions and exclusions
sources.summary: Official establishment classifications support business-role and detailed-industry exception review; they do not establish accounting treatments.

sources.title: IAS 38: public intangible-asset and research/development overview
sources.summary: The overview distinguishes research expenditure from development meeting specified recognition criteria, and finite-life amortization from annual impairment testing of indefinite-life intangible assets.

sources.title: GASB 34: governmental funds and government-wide reconciliation
sources.summary: Selected operative paragraphs distinguish the governmental-fund measurement basis from government-wide accrual reporting and require reconciliations for capital assets, long-term obligations and other differences.

sources.title: ASU 2025-06 Internal-Use Software: Targeted Improvements
sources.summary: The FASB update removes sequential project stages, starts capitalization when management authorizes and commits funding and completion/use is probable, requires consideration of significant development uncertainty, and leaves external-use software in Subtopic 985-20. The summary states the effective date and three transition approaches.

sources.title: Principal versus Agent: Software Reseller—IFRS 15 (Final May 2022 Agenda Decision)
sources.summary: The final decision describes the software-reseller fact pattern and concludes IFRS 15 provides an adequate basis to determine principal or agent; it does not decide every reseller’s role. It identifies manufacturer responsibility for functionality and issuance, reseller customer and unaccepted-licence responsibilities, no pre-order pool inventory risk, post-issue acceptance risk and pricing discretion.

sources.title: FASB staff educational paper: construction retainage presentation
sources.summary: Conditional retainage participates in the net contract position. Unconditional receivables remain separate; one contract does not report both a contract asset and liability.

sources.title: GAO-25-107258: construction estimate and final-cost evidence
sources.summary: GAO examined 252 fixed-price construction subcontracts completed in FY2023. Final costs exceeded initial estimates by $37.5 million; $35.6 million arose after award.

sources.title: ASBCA 51759: same-job billing, retainage and supplier-payment evidence
sources.summary: Published findings connect a construction contract, modifications, invoices and payments to an identified job; the underlying complete ledger and exhibits are not supplied.
sources.publisher: Armed Services Board of Contract Appeals

sources.title: FASB ASU 2018-08: contributions, exchange transactions and conditions
sources.summary: FASB amendment distinguishes reciprocal exchange transactions from contributions and makes a contribution conditional only when an agreement includes both a barrier and a right of return or release.

sources.title: FASB ASU 2016-14: NFP presentation, restrictions and functional expenses
sources.summary: FASB amendment establishes two net-asset classes, donor-restriction release presentation, liquidity disclosures, endowment disclosures and expense reporting by nature and function for not-for-profit entities.

sources.title: ASU 2016-08: principal-versus-agent presentation
sources.summary: Amends Topic 606 to clarify that principal-versus-agent presentation turns on whether the entity controls a specified good or service before transfer; the current Codification remains authoritative.

sources.title: ASU 2015-11: inventory measured at lower of cost and net realizable value
sources.summary: Amends Topic 330 so inventory measured by methods other than LIFO or the retail method, including FIFO or average cost, is subsequently measured at the lower of cost and net realizable value; scope and transition are explicit.

sources.title: Concepts Statement 8, Chapter 4: elements and accrual accounting
sources.summary: Provides non-authoritative conceptual definitions of liabilities, revenues, expenses and accrual accounting, including the distinction between present obligations and future business risks.

sources.title: FSA Handbook 2025-2026: Disbursing Title IV funds
sources.summary: Program administration for eligible institutions, not accounting recognition authority.

sources.title: FSA Handbook 2025-2026: Withdrawal and return of Title IV funds
sources.summary: The 2025-2026 program-year guidance is not a determination of later July2026 rule applicability.

sources.title: GASB Statement 35: Public colleges and universities
sources.summary: Original November1999 statement, not current consolidated GASB guidance; later amendments require separate review.

sources.title: FERC electric utility Uniform System of Accounts
sources.summary: Part 101 applies to specified Federal Power Act utilities and licensees. Account 182.3 concerns regulatory-created assets arising from ratemaking actions.
sources.publisher: FERC; Office of the Federal Register

sources.title: ONRR minerals revenue reporting: Release4.5 field boundaries
sources.summary: Dated reporting instructions separate sale quantities, value, royalty rate and allowances. They do not establish private royalty ownership or GAAP revenue.

sources.title: RMA Common Crop Insurance Policy Basic Provisions 26-BR
sources.summary: Production and acreage reports identify shares, units, gross/net output and deductions. Loss notices and supporting production evidence are separate from sale records and ledger recognition.

sources.title: NOAA commercial fisheries landings: quantity and value documentation
sources.summary: Landing populations use dealer/fisher records including trip tickets. Landed quantity and value are evidence categories; they do not establish inventory valuation or ownership of uncaught fish.

sources.title: NOAA Catch Shares: allocation and program boundaries
sources.summary: Catch-share arrangements allocate allowable catch. The accounting for an acquired quota/access right requires its own legal and measurement analysis.

sources.title: US Forest Service FS-2400-4 timber sale contract
sources.summary: The model separates timber title, payment and removal. A logging-service provider and a purchaser of timber rights require distinct contract and quantity populations.

sources.title: FASB ASU 2016-13: Measurement of Credit Losses on Financial Instruments
sources.summary: The Update replaces the incurred-loss model with an expected-credit-loss model for financial assets within its scope and requires reasonable and supportable information without prescribing one estimation method.

sources.title: ASU 2016-04: breakage for prepaid stored-value products
sources.summary: Adds a narrow Topic 405 breakage model for in-scope prepaid stored-value product liabilities, including gift cards, while excluding unclaimed-property and other scoped cases.

sources.title: FERC Accounting Questions and Answers
sources.summary: FERC staff Q&A page for jurisdictional public utilities, licensees, natural gas companies and oil pipeline companies, including plant-related accounting and limits on the binding force of informal answers.

sources.title: Accounting for settlement amounts in Account 555, Purchased Power
sources.summary: FERC Chief Accountant guidance distinguishing purchased power and eligible net exchange settlements from distinct purchases and sales that must be recorded gross.

sources.title: ASU 2016-02: Leases
sources.summary: The issued FASB update supplies the bounded Topic 842 lease-identification, lessee commencement, remeasurement and modification passages used by the synthetic lessee workflow. Current Codification and later amendments control.

sources.title: FASB ASU 2020-05: deferred lease effective dates for specified entities
sources.summary: The amendment further defers the specified nonpublic lease adoption dates after ASU2019-10. A2026 private-company analysis must establish its adoption and elections rather than repeat the original2016 issuance schedule.

sources.title: 49 CFR Part 371, Brokers of Property
sources.summary: Federal broker definition, transaction records, compensation and carrier-payment fields, retention, misrepresentation boundary, and segregated brokerage accounting.

sources.title: 49 CFR 377.203, Extension of Credit to Shippers
sources.summary: Freight-bill presentation and credit timing used as billing and receivable evidence.

sources.title: FMCSA Regulations and Enforcement, Part 370 claims route
sources.summary: Official FMCSA index identifying Part 370 as the claims and salvage rule for loss and damage claims.

sources.title: Uniform Commercial Code Article 7, Documents of Title (2003)
sources.summary: Model-law framework for warehouse receipts, bills of lading, bailees and custodial goods, with a state-enactment boundary.

sources.title: 49 CFR Part 374, regular-route passenger ticketing and service
sources.summary: For the selected regular-route passenger role, schedules and ticket/refund terms supply evidence distinct from freight billing. Unused-ticket refunds follow the governing tariff; fare receipts alone do not establish accounting recognition.

sources.title: ASU 2016-10: Identifying Performance Obligations and Licensing
sources.summary: FASB amendments clarify identifying separate performance obligations and license revenue distinctions under Topic 606, including right-to-use versus right-to-access licenses.

sources.title: 47 CFR Part 32: Uniform System of Accounts for Telecommunications Companies
sources.summary: FCC Part 32 is a federal telecommunications accounting and recordkeeping regime for specified carriers; sections 32.11 and 32.14 define applicability and regulated versus nonregulated accounting boundaries.
sources.publisher: Federal Communications Commission; Office of the Federal Register

sources.title: 17 USC Chapter 3: copyright duration and terminal dates
sources.summary: The US Code provides duration rules for copyrighted works, including life-plus-70, work-made-for-hire and terminal-year rules; a contractual license term still requires the actual agreement and rights chain.
sources.publisher: Office of the Law Revision Counsel, U.S. House of Representatives

sources.title: Illinois Uniform Prudent Management of Institutional Funds Act, 760 ILCS 51
sources.summary: Selected Illinois institutional-fund provisions provide a state-law routing example for donor instruments, prudent endowment management, modification of restrictions and no-hindsight review; they are not a national nonprofit endowment rule.

sources.title: IRS Publication 598: unrelated business income boundaries for colleges and universities
sources.summary: IRS Publication 598 explains the federal unrelated-business boundary for regularly conducted activities of exempt organizations, including state and municipal colleges and universities; it is a tax boundary, not a US GAAP revenue-recognition authority.

sources.title: ARB 51 as amended by FAS 160: historical consolidation procedures
sources.summary: Historical amended consolidation procedures identify the group as one economic entity and address intercompany balances, transactions and parent-company presentation.
sources.publisher: AICPA Committee on Accounting Procedure; amended text hosted by FASB

sources.title: 2025 controlled-services regulation: allocation, benefit and shareholder activities
sources.summary: Dated federal tax text connects controlled services to a recipient benefit, identifies cost-allocation considerations and distinguishes shareholder or passive association activities.
sources.publisher: Internal Revenue Service and Treasury via GovInfo

sources.title: ASU 2010-23: charity-care cost disclosure
sources.summary: The issued amendment measures charity-care disclosure using direct and indirect costs and separately discloses funding received to support that care.

sources.title: CMS T-MSIS v4 sub-capitation payments and encounters
sources.summary: CMS separates state capitation, downstream sub-capitation and utilization encounters, including rendering-provider and payment-recipient identity.

sources.title: FASB Statement 67: costs and initial rental operations of real estate projects
sources.summary: Historical FASB guidance establishes bounded routes for preacquisition, project, allocation, rent and recoverability costs for real estate projects. It is dated source evidence, not current consolidated GAAP.

sources.title: FASB Statement 66: accounting for sales of real estate
sources.summary: Historical FASB guidance distinguishes retail land sales from other real estate sales and conditions full-accrual recognition on consummation, collectibility, investment, subordination and continuing involvement. It is not a current universal Topic 606 conclusion.

sources.title: IRS tip recordkeeping, employer reporting and service charges
sources.summary: The IRS distinguishes discretionary customer tips from mandatory service charges and identifies employer tax and reporting duties.

sources.title: ASU 2021-02: nonpublic franchisor pre-opening service expedient
sources.summary: The issued amendment offers an eligible nonpublic franchisor a limited expedient for identifying specified pre-opening services as distinct from a franchise license.

sources.title: Publication 15-A (2026), Employer’s Supplemental Tax Guide
sources.summary: IRS 15-A supplies federal worker-classification and withholding context: the substance of control, financial factors and relationship matters, and labels alone do not decide employee status.

sources.title: IRS exempt-organization gaming and unrelated business taxable income
sources.summary: IRS guidance routes exempt-organization gaming through unrelated-business-income factors and exceptions, including bingo, volunteer labor, public entertainment and member or nonmember distinctions. It also calls for separate gross gaming receipts and prize/disbursement records.

questions.question: When a bundle combines software access, hosting, telecom or content, how should provider presentation stay separate from customer software expenditure?
questions.scope: Selected US provider and customer roles under US GAAP; bundle includes hosted access, licensed content, connectivity or implementation; reseller/intermediary counterexample included.
questions.answer: Decompose the provider bundle using the contract and role evidence, then assess whether the provider controls the promised service before transfer. The provider revenue analysis is separate from the customer’s accounting for acquired software, hosting fees or implementation costs. A reseller invoice is not automatically gross revenue, and a customer’s prepaid or implementation amount is not automatically the provider’s earned revenue.

questions.question: When does a management-service charge differ from passive holding activity?
questions.scope: US domestic registrant parent and assumed controlled operating subsidiary; 2025 synthetic close; separate financial-reporting and federal tax purposes.
questions.answer: Document the actual service and recipient benefit before choosing a cost driver. The original allocation case uses documented processing units, retains the renderer share and separates internal allocation from tax-method and markup conclusions. The charge and receipt are reciprocal entity entries, then eliminated within the assumed group.

For a real-estate sale branch, FAS 66 paragraphs 3-6 provide dated evidence about consummation, collectibility, buyer investment, subordination and continuing involvement. questions.answer: Classify the purchased item, promise and entity role before posting. A customer invoice or reimbursement label does not establish gross or net presentation; principal-versus-agent control, contract terms and who obtains the service determine the route, while incurred cost and recoverability remain separately evidenced.

questions.question: How should a fixed-fee or time-and-material project connect time, WIP, unbilled revenue and billing?
questions.scope: Selected US professional, scientific and technical service roles under the stated framework and effective period; legal client-fund route is California only when governing law is established.
questions.answer: Use approved time, cost-to-complete and contract-right evidence to select and measure the performance obligation. questions.question: How should subcontractor costs and staffing arrangements be separated?
questions.scope: Selected US professional, scientific and technical service roles under the stated framework and effective period; legal client-fund route is California only when governing law is established.

sources.title: FASB Accounting Standards Codification
sources.summary: The authoritative US GAAP source. Agent-produced accounting remains subject to the same recognition, measurement, presentation, and disclosure requirements.

sources.title: Internal Control: Integrated Framework
sources.summary: The five-component, 17-principle foundation for governing agent-enabled financial processes and control activities.

sources.title: IFRS 15, Revenue from Contracts with Customers
sources.summary: Official revenue-recognition anchor. Apply current endorsed text and entity facts; the standard does not grant billing, posting, or approval authority.

sources.title: IAS 2, Inventories
sources.summary: Official inventory-cost, cost-formula, net-realizable-value, and write-down anchor. Physical existence, condition, policy, and current evidence remain fact-specific.

sources.title: AI Agents for Cash Management in Payment Systems
sources.summary: Tests prompt-based agent recommendations under liquidity shocks and competing priorities. The simulation does not establish safe autonomous operation, and the authors call for regulatory and policy safeguards.
sources.publisher: Bank for International Settlements and Bank of Canada researchers

sources.title: ASU 2018-15: Customer's Accounting for Implementation Costs in a Cloud Computing Arrangement
sources.summary: Addresses capitalization, expense, amortization, impairment, and presentation of implementation costs in service-contract cloud arrangements. The issued update is not a substitute for the current Codification or a fact-specific conclusion.

sources.title: FOCUS Specification 1.4
sources.summary: Defines a common schema and minimum requirements for billing data supporting allocation, chargeback, budgets, and forecasting. It is an operational data contract, not GAAP, and provider conformance and version pinning still require validation.

sources.title: Accounting Matters
sources.summary: Indexes FERC Uniform Systems of Accounts, forms, orders, and Chief Accountant guidance for electric, gas, and oil-pipeline entities. These regulatory requirements are industry-specific and do not establish an AI-agent design.

sources.title: Retail Industry Audit Technique Guide
sources.summary: Covers receipts, rebates, chargebacks, gift cards, inventory methods, point-of-sale records, online retail, loyalty programs, and cost of goods sold. It is an examiner aid, not law, GAAP, or agent-performance evidence.

sources.title: 2 CFR Part 200, Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards
sources.summary: Current eCFR Part 200 requires federal-award costs to be necessary, reasonable, allocable, consistently treated, GAAP-based where applicable, documented, and not double charged; §§200.302, 200.328, 200.329 and 200.501 provide selected financial-management, reporting, performance-monitoring and audit-routing requirements. It is an external federal-award rule, not a general internal management-accounting standard.
sources.publisher: US Office of Management and Budget and eCFR

sources.title: Publication 15 (2026), Circular E, Employer’s Tax Guide
sources.summary: The annual employer guide provides the federal payroll-tax context for withholding, deposits, reporting, and recordkeeping.

sources.title: FFIEC 051 Call Report instructions — December 2025
sources.summary: Quarterly bank-reporting instructions define eligibility, report schedules and accounting glossary context.

sources.title: OCC Bank Accounting Advisory Series — 2026
sources.summary: OCC staff interpretations address banking accounting fact patterns and regulatory-reporting questions.
sources.publisher: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency

sources.title: WIP schedules: blueprints for solid construction accounting
sources.summary: Explains how a contractor WIP schedule brings together contract value, estimated costs, costs incurred, earned revenue and billing.

sources.title: ASU 2014-09: original revenue recognition amendments, Section A
sources.summary: Sets out over-time criteria, progress measurement and contract-balance presentation; input measures may require adjustment for costs that do not depict performance.

sources.title: Texas real property repair, remodeling and construction tax
sources.summary: Tax treatment varies with the work and contract: Texas distinguishes new construction from nonresidential repair and distinguishes contractor consumption from sales of incorporated materials.

sources.title: California Publication 9: construction and building contractors
sources.summary: Separates materials, fixtures and machinery when determining whether contractors act as consumers or retailers.
sources.publisher: California Department of Tax and Fee Administration

sources.title: Washington WAC 458-20-170: construction on real property
sources.summary: Distinguishes prime contracting, subcontracting and speculative building, with different B&O and sales/use-tax consequences.

sources.title: New York sales and use tax: contractors
sources.summary: Distinguishes qualifying capital improvements from taxable repair and maintenance, and addresses contractor purchases and capital-improvement certificates.
sources.publisher: New York State Department of Taxation and Finance

sources.title: Florida TAA 22A-015: contractor consumption and a historical exemption
sources.summary: Illustrates Florida’s contractor-consumer analysis through a particular window and door contract and a time-limited sales-tax exemption.

sources.title: Davis-Bacon weekly certified payroll: WH-347 instructions
sources.summary: Covered contractors submit weekly certified payroll information and a signed statement of compliance; WH-347 is an optional form for supplying required information.

sources.title: California public works certified payroll reporting
sources.summary: Describes certified payroll reporting for most California public works projects, with specified exemptions and electronic reporting requirements.

sources.title: Texas Government Code Chapter 2251: payment for goods and services
sources.summary: Provides public-sector payment rules that require identifying the government purchaser, invoice and contract circumstances.

sources.title: MTC model construction contractor apportionment regulation
sources.summary: Illustrates why long-term contract income and project activity can span multiple states and tax years.

sources.title: Financial reporting developments: revenue from contracts with customers, September 2026
sources.summary: Current technical interpretation used to cross-check selected ASC 606 requirements and distinguish modifications, progress inputs and contract balances.

sources.title: Revenue recognition handbook, December 2025: loss-contract scope
sources.summary: Selected loss-contract chapter distinguishes construction and production contracts from excluded ordinary goods and service arrangements.

sources.title: 2022 NAICS United States manual: industry definitions and exclusions
sources.summary: Official establishment classifications support business-role and detailed-industry exception review; they do not establish accounting treatments.

sources.title: GASB 34: governmental funds and government-wide reconciliation
sources.summary: Selected operative paragraphs distinguish the governmental-fund measurement basis from government-wide accrual reporting and require reconciliations for capital assets, long-term obligations and other differences.

sources.title: Inventory accounting: IFRS Accounting Standards vs US GAAP
sources.summary: KPMG’s current comparison states that IAS 2 prohibits LIFO, generally uses lower of cost and NRV, and requires reversal of write-downs up to original cost; US GAAP permits LIFO and prohibits reversals, with market measurement for LIFO/retail inventories.

sources.title: Revenue handbook 2025: principal versus agent and consignment
sources.summary: Interpretive handbook material was used for application context; primary IFRS 15 authority remains the cited standard source.

sources.title: Principal versus Agent: Software Reseller—IFRS 15 (Final May 2022 Agenda Decision)
sources.summary: The final decision describes the software-reseller fact pattern and concludes IFRS 15 provides an adequate basis to determine principal or agent; it does not decide every reseller’s role. It identifies manufacturer responsibility for functionality and issuance, reseller customer and unaccepted-licence responsibilities, no pre-order pool inventory risk, post-issue acceptance risk and pricing discretion.

sources.title: California Tax Guide for Construction Contractors
sources.summary: CDTFA treats contractors as consumers of materials and retailers of fixtures; permit and use-tax exceptions depend on contract and customer facts.

sources.title: HMRC VAT domestic reverse charge technical guide
sources.summary: Sections cover CIS/VAT registration, end-user notification, labour-only subcontractors, mixed supplies and 5% disregard.

sources.title: GST/HST registrants guide RC4022
sources.summary: GST/HST registration, taxable supplies, input tax credits and filing/remittance guidance for registrants.

sources.title: FASB staff educational paper: construction retainage presentation
sources.summary: Conditional retainage participates in the net contract position. Unconditional receivables remain separate; one contract does not report both a contract asset and liability.

sources.title: GAO-25-107258: construction estimate and final-cost evidence
sources.summary: GAO examined 252 fixed-price construction subcontracts completed in FY2023. Final costs exceeded initial estimates by $37.5 million; $35.6 million arose after award.

sources.title: ASBCA 51759: same-job billing, retainage and supplier-payment evidence
sources.summary: Published findings connect a construction contract, modifications, invoices and payments to an identified job; the underlying complete ledger and exhibits are not supplied.
sources.publisher: Armed Services Board of Contract Appeals

sources.title: FASB ASU 2018-08: contributions, exchange transactions and conditions
sources.summary: FASB amendment distinguishes reciprocal exchange transactions from contributions and makes a contribution conditional only when an agreement includes both a barrier and a right of return or release.

sources.title: FASB ASU 2016-14: NFP presentation, restrictions and functional expenses
sources.summary: FASB amendment establishes two net-asset classes, donor-restriction release presentation, liquidity disclosures, endowment disclosures and expense reporting by nature and function for not-for-profit entities.

sources.title: ASU 2016-08: principal-versus-agent presentation
sources.summary: Amends Topic 606 to clarify that principal-versus-agent presentation turns on whether the entity controls a specified good or service before transfer; the current Codification remains authoritative.

sources.title: ASU 2015-11: inventory measured at lower of cost and net realizable value
sources.summary: Amends Topic 330 so inventory measured by methods other than LIFO or the retail method, including FIFO or average cost, is subsequently measured at the lower of cost and net realizable value; scope and transition are explicit.

sources.title: Concepts Statement 8, Chapter 4: elements and accrual accounting
sources.summary: Provides non-authoritative conceptual definitions of liabilities, revenues, expenses and accrual accounting, including the distinction between present obligations and future business risks.

sources.title: FASB December 18, 2024 board handout: Topic 330 inventory measurement
sources.summary: A FASB staff board handout describes ASC 330-10-30-1 as using cost as the primary inventory measurement basis and explains that acquisition and production costs bring inventory to its existing condition and location.
sources.source_type: FASB staff board meeting handout; non-authoritative

sources.title: FSA Handbook 2025-2026: Disbursing Title IV funds
sources.summary: Program administration for eligible institutions, not accounting recognition authority.

sources.title: FSA Handbook 2025-2026: Withdrawal and return of Title IV funds
sources.summary: The 2025-2026 program-year guidance is not a determination of later July2026 rule applicability.

sources.title: GASB Statement 35: Public colleges and universities
sources.summary: Original November1999 statement, not current consolidated GASB guidance; later amendments require separate review.

sources.title: FERC electric utility Uniform System of Accounts
sources.summary: Part 101 applies to specified Federal Power Act utilities and licensees. Account 182.3 concerns regulatory-created assets arising from ratemaking actions.
sources.publisher: FERC; Office of the Federal Register

sources.title: ONRR minerals revenue reporting: Release4.5 field boundaries
sources.summary: Dated reporting instructions separate sale quantities, value, royalty rate and allowances. They do not establish private royalty ownership or GAAP revenue.

sources.title: RMA Common Crop Insurance Policy Basic Provisions 26-BR
sources.summary: Production and acreage reports identify shares, units, gross/net output and deductions. Loss notices and supporting production evidence are separate from sale records and ledger recognition.

sources.title: NOAA commercial fisheries landings: quantity and value documentation
sources.summary: Landing populations use dealer/fisher records including trip tickets. Landed quantity and value are evidence categories; they do not establish inventory valuation or ownership of uncaught fish.

sources.title: NOAA Catch Shares: allocation and program boundaries
sources.summary: Catch-share arrangements allocate allowable catch. The accounting for an acquired quota/access right requires its own legal and measurement analysis.

sources.title: US Forest Service FS-2400-4 timber sale contract
sources.summary: The model separates timber title, payment and removal. A logging-service provider and a purchaser of timber rights require distinct contract and quantity populations.

sources.title: FASB Accounting Standards Codification
sources.summary: The authoritative US GAAP source. Agent-produced accounting remains subject to the same recognition, measurement, presentation, and disclosure requirements.

sources.title: IAS 2, Inventories
sources.summary: Official inventory-cost, cost-formula, net-realizable-value, and write-down anchor. Physical existence, condition, policy, and current evidence remain fact-specific.

sources.title: IAS 36, Impairment of Assets
sources.summary: Official impairment-indicator, recoverable-amount, testing, and write-down anchor. Valuation inputs, cash-generating-unit scope, sensitivity, and conclusions remain accountable judgments.

sources.title: SEC Financial Reporting Manual
sources.summary: SEC staff practice and interpretation locator. It is expressly informal and nonauthoritative; statutes, rules, releases, and current accounting standards control.

sources.title: Standards for Internal Control in the Federal Government, 2025 Green Book
sources.summary: Current federal internal-control standard covering authority, risk, control activities, information, monitoring, fraud, and remediation. Outside federal scope, use it as guidance rather than binding law.

sources.title: GAO Financial Audit Manual
sources.summary: Federal financial-audit methodology and current references. Do not generalize its procedures or authority to private entities without an applicable basis.

sources.title: IFRS S2, Climate-related Disclosures
sources.summary: Covers climate risks and opportunities, governance, strategy, risk management, metrics, and industry-based guidance. It is climate-specific and does not replace accounting, assurance, or local disclosure requirements.

sources.title: Accounting Matters
sources.summary: Indexes FERC Uniform Systems of Accounts, forms, orders, and Chief Accountant guidance for electric, gas, and oil-pipeline entities. These regulatory requirements are industry-specific and do not establish an AI-agent design.

sources.title: 2 CFR Part 200, Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards
sources.summary: Current eCFR Part 200 requires federal-award costs to be necessary, reasonable, allocable, consistently treated, GAAP-based where applicable, documented, and not double charged; §§200.302, 200.328, 200.329 and 200.501 provide selected financial-management, reporting, performance-monitoring and audit-routing requirements. It is an external federal-award rule, not a general internal management-accounting standard.
sources.publisher: US Office of Management and Budget and eCFR

sources.title: GASB Statement No. 96, Subscription-Based Information Technology Arrangements
sources.summary: Addresses subscription liabilities and assets, implementation stages, capitalization, amortization, and disclosures for government SBITAs. It is public-sector accounting authority, not AI guidance.

sources.title: FFIEC 051 Call Report instructions — December 2025
sources.summary: Quarterly bank-reporting instructions define eligibility, report schedules and accounting glossary context.

sources.title: NAIC statutory accounting hierarchy and AP&P Manual
sources.summary: NAIC describes the authority hierarchy behind insurer statutory financial reporting.

sources.title: CMS hospital cost-report instructions — Transmittal 25
sources.summary: The 2026 hospital cost-report revision records worksheet changes and separate electronic-specification effective dates.

sources.title: ASU 2014-09: original revenue recognition amendments, Section A
sources.summary: Sets out over-time criteria, progress measurement and contract-balance presentation; input measures may require adjustment for costs that do not depict performance.

sources.title: 2022 NAICS United States manual: industry definitions and exclusions
sources.summary: Official establishment classifications support business-role and detailed-industry exception review; they do not establish accounting treatments.

sources.title: IAS 37: public provisions, contingencies and onerous-contract overview
sources.summary: The overview distinguishes uncertain obligations, contingent liabilities and contingent assets. It identifies restoration and warranty examples and separates onerous contracts from future operating losses without a present obligation.

sources.title: GASB 34: governmental funds and government-wide reconciliation
sources.summary: Selected operative paragraphs distinguish the governmental-fund measurement basis from government-wide accrual reporting and require reconciliations for capital assets, long-term obligations and other differences.

sources.title: GASB 103: reporting model changes and budget comparison requirements
sources.summary: The selected amendments require budget comparison information in required supplementary information, with original-to-final and final-to-actual variances, and apply for fiscal years beginning after June 15, 2025.

sources.title: SFFAS 34: federal GAAP hierarchy and limited FASB reporting exceptions
sources.summary: The standard orders sources of federal accounting guidance, addresses missing guidance and retains limited circumstances in which a federal entity reports under FASB standards.

sources.title: SFFAS 53: budget and accrual reconciliation for federal component entities
sources.summary: The budget and accrual reconciliation starts with net cost and explains adjustments to net outlays, including depreciation, capital acquisitions and timing differences. It distinguishes component reporting from the consolidated US government report.

sources.title: IAS 41 Agriculture
sources.summary: The IFRS Foundation page states IAS 41 covers managed biological transformation and harvest, measures other biological assets and produce at fair value less costs to sell, and excludes post-harvest processing.

sources.title: IFRS 6 Exploration for and Evaluation of Mineral Resources
sources.summary: The IFRS Foundation page identifies IFRS 6 as the exploration and evaluation standard; detailed treatment requires the licensed text.

sources.title: 42 CFR 413.24 adequate cost data and cost finding
sources.summary: The current eCFR requires providers receiving payment on a reimbursable-cost basis to provide adequate cost data based on financial and statistical records verifiable by qualified auditors; defines cost finding as recasting account data through direct allocation and indirect proration; and requires adequate data from provider records. Paragraph (f)(2)(i) sets the due date at the last day of the fifth month after the covered period (or 150 days when the period ends other than month-end); (f)(2)(ii) limits contractor extensions to operations significantly adversely affected by extraordinary circumstances beyond the provider’s control. The rule lists post-period cost-finding methods and exceptions, so a claims or encounter population cannot simply be treated as the cost ledger.
sources.publisher: Office of the Federal Register; HHS

sources.title: CMS Provider Reimbursement Manual 2552-10 hospital cost report instructions
sources.summary: The CMS 2552-10 instructions state that filing is mandatory, identify the form as effective for hospitals and hospital health care complexes with periods beginning on or after May 1, 2010, and use the certification requiring the report and balance sheet/statement of revenues and expenses to be true, correct, complete and prepared from provider books and records. The Worksheet S-2 Part I identifies the provider CCN, component provider types, payment system columns and cost-reporting period, showing why entity/component and period fields are required before reconciling populations.

sources.title: FASB ASU 2018-08: contributions, exchange transactions and conditions
sources.summary: FASB amendment distinguishes reciprocal exchange transactions from contributions and makes a contribution conditional only when an agreement includes both a barrier and a right of return or release.

sources.title: ASU 2016-08: principal-versus-agent presentation
sources.summary: Amends Topic 606 to clarify that principal-versus-agent presentation turns on whether the entity controls a specified good or service before transfer; the current Codification remains authoritative.

sources.title: ASU 2015-11: inventory measured at lower of cost and net realizable value
sources.summary: Amends Topic 330 so inventory measured by methods other than LIFO or the retail method, including FIFO or average cost, is subsequently measured at the lower of cost and net realizable value; scope and transition are explicit.

sources.title: GASB Statement 35: Public colleges and universities
sources.summary: Original November1999 statement, not current consolidated GASB guidance; later amendments require separate review.

sources.title: FERC electric utility Uniform System of Accounts
sources.summary: Part 101 applies to specified Federal Power Act utilities and licensees. Account 182.3 concerns regulatory-created assets arising from ratemaking actions.
sources.publisher: FERC; Office of the Federal Register

sources.title: SEC investment adviser client custody rule
sources.summary: Covered advisers must use qualified custodians, client notices and statements, and independent verification subject to the rule exceptions. Custody and ownership are separate facts.
sources.publisher: SEC; Office of the Federal Register

sources.title: SEC oil and gas accounting method boundaries, 2025 CFR
sources.summary: The successful-efforts route points to ASC 932. Full-cost rules distinguish country cost centers, acquisition/exploration/development capitalization, amortization, ceiling limits and production expense.

sources.title: NAIC statutory accounting and state practice boundaries
sources.summary: The AP&P framework supports insurer statutory reporting; state prescribed and permitted practices can differ. Statutory solvency reporting is a distinct reporting purpose.

sources.title: ONRR minerals revenue reporting: Release4.5 field boundaries
sources.summary: Dated reporting instructions separate sale quantities, value, royalty rate and allowances. They do not establish private royalty ownership or GAAP revenue.

sources.title: FASB Statement143: historical retirement-obligation recognition boundary
sources.summary: The historical statement distinguishes qualifying retirement obligations from improper-operation remediation and describes liability recognition and associated retirement costs. This record is historical evidence, not current consolidated ASC410.

sources.title: SEC staff mining letter: historical exploration and development distinction
sources.summary: A 2001 SEC staff request for a mining accounting project raises exploration capitalization and development-stage distinctions. It is historical staff analysis, not a replacement for current US GAAP or current mining disclosure rules.
sources.publisher: Securities and Exchange Commission, Office of the Chief Accountant

sources.title: SEC oil and gas reporting: dated full-cost and successful-efforts boundaries
sources.summary: The April 2025 rule distinguishes successful-efforts reporting from a full-cost method with country cost centers and a defined amortization base. It does not establish a policy for all mining activities.

sources.title: RMA Common Crop Insurance Policy Basic Provisions 26-BR
sources.summary: Production and acreage reports identify shares, units, gross/net output and deductions. Loss notices and supporting production evidence are separate from sale records and ledger recognition.

sources.title: NOAA commercial fisheries landings: quantity and value documentation
sources.summary: Landing populations use dealer/fisher records including trip tickets. Landed quantity and value are evidence categories; they do not establish inventory valuation or ownership of uncaught fish.

sources.title: NOAA Catch Shares: allocation and program boundaries
sources.summary: Catch-share arrangements allocate allowable catch. The accounting for an acquired quota/access right requires its own legal and measurement analysis.

sources.title: US Forest Service FS-2400-4 timber sale contract
sources.summary: The model separates timber title, payment and removal. A logging-service provider and a purchaser of timber rights require distinct contract and quantity populations.

sources.title: USDA ARMS documentation: production and farm financial populations
sources.summary: The survey distinguishes acreage, output, commodity contracts, custom work, input spending, assets and debt. Those categories inform evidence intake without supplying entity-level GAAP cost eligibility.

sources.title: FASB Statement 5: loss-contingency research
sources.summary: Accrual depends on a probable incurred loss and reasonable estimation. Possible additional losses have separate disclosure requirements; general business-risk reserves are inappropriate.

sources.title: FASB Statement 143: retirement versus remediation
sources.summary: Legal retirement duties from normal asset operation are distinguished from improper-operation remediation. The model includes fair-value recognition, capitalized retirement cost, accretion, revisions and settlements.

sources.title: SEC SAB Topic 5.Y: product and environmental claims
sources.summary: Registrant disclosures address estimation uncertainty, recoverability and carrier solvency. A contested indemnification claim carries a rebuttable presumption against recognizing a recovery asset.
sources.publisher: US Securities and Exchange Commission staff

sources.title: EPA Superfund liability: responsible-party evidence
sources.summary: EPA identifies potentially responsible ownership, operation, arrangement and transport roles and explains strict, retroactive and joint-and-several liability. This is a legal-fact research route, not a GAAP recognition decision.

sources.title: ASU 2016-04: breakage for prepaid stored-value products
sources.summary: Adds a narrow Topic 405 breakage model for in-scope prepaid stored-value product liabilities, including gift cards, while excluding unclaimed-property and other scoped cases.

sources.title: FERC Accounting Questions and Answers
sources.summary: FERC staff Q&A page for jurisdictional public utilities, licensees, natural gas companies and oil pipeline companies, including plant-related accounting and limits on the binding force of informal answers.

sources.title: FASB Statement No. 143: Accounting for Asset Retirement Obligations
sources.summary: Official FASB superseded-standard summary describing the historical recognition, initial measurement, capitalization, accretion and depreciation model for qualifying legal asset-retirement obligations.

sources.title: IRS Publication 598: unrelated business income boundaries for colleges and universities
sources.summary: IRS Publication 598 explains the federal unrelated-business boundary for regularly conducted activities of exempt organizations, including state and municipal colleges and universities; it is a tax boundary, not a US GAAP revenue-recognition authority.

sources.title: EPA hazardous-waste TSDF financial assurance
sources.summary: EPA describes third-party closure and post-closure estimates, annual inflation updates and assurance mechanisms for hazardous-waste facility owners/operators.
